a23.speaker: Riaan van Rooyen, spokesperson for Headsprings Investments (HI)
a23.name: Riaan van Rooyen
a23.title: spokesperson for Headsprings Investments (HI)
a23.speech: Corrected earlier reports months later, stating that the company is a 100%-Namibia-registered exploration company owned by the Russian company "Uranium One" (UO).

a23.speaker: Dr. Roy Miller, retired geologist and former head of Namibia's Geological Survey, Ministry of Mines and Energy
a23.name: Dr. Roy Miller
a23.title: retired geologist and former head of Namibia's Geological Survey, Ministry of Mines and Energy
a23.speech: Said the planned closed water-loop system is wishful thinking in an aquifer made up of various interconnected water-bearing layers; as a former mining engineer, said he could not follow HI's reasoning in an area so dependent on this single reliable water resource, the Stampriet Aquifer.

a23.speaker: Headsprings Investments (HI)
a23.name: Headsprings Investments (HI)
a23.speech: Regards in-situ leaching as the only alternative to open-pit and shaft mining, which it says are "not practicable options"; says it is confident it can establish a closed water loop because there is sufficient water in the targeted Auob 3 aquifer and it flows slowly enough.

a23.speaker: Activists, Dr. Roy Miller, and SAUMA (Stampriet Aquifer Uranium Mining Association)
a23.name: Activists
a23.title: Dr. Roy Miller, and SAUMA (Stampriet Aquifer Uranium Mining Association)
a23.speech: Argue that the Ministry of Environment should not grant the company an environmental clearance for its test project, warning that even this initial step poses a massive threat to the water body, which UNESCO describes as uniquely important for this part of Namibia and neighboring Botswana.

a189.speaker: Bajabulile Swazi Tshabalala, AfDB senior vice president and presidential candidate (South Africa)
a189.name: Bajabulile Swazi Tshabalala
a189.title: AfDB senior vice president and presidential candidate (South Africa)
a189.speech: Argued for infrastructure-led regional integration: "Closing this infrastructure gap will facilitate greater regional integration ... especially to leverage the [African] Continental Free Trade Area and also to create jobs."

a189.speaker: Bajabulile Swazi Tshabalala, AfDB presidential candidate
a189.name: Bajabulile Swazi Tshabalala
a189.title: AfDB presidential candidate
a189.speech: On addressing Africa's growing debt burden, she added, "We must work with countries ... to ensure that their debt is used for investment, not for consumption, because investment is what will generate a future income."

a189.speaker: Samuel Munzele Maimbo, former World Bank official and AfDB vice president for regional development, presidential candidate (Zambia)
a189.name: Samuel Munzele Maimbo
a189.title: former World Bank official and AfDB vice president for regional development, presidential candidate (Zambia)
a189.speech: Emphasized the need for more transparency and realism in strategic planning: "I will not be issuing a 10-year strategy in my last year of my presidency. Instead, I'll be writing a detailed report of where we succeeded and even more details on where we failed." He also pushed for more equitable treatment of African debt, saying, "We must broaden [debt] instrument, increase the revenue sources of our governments, [and] reduce the risk premium that we unfairly pay across the continent."

a189.speaker: Amadou Hott, Senegal's former minister of economy and planning and former AfDB vice president, presidential candidate
a189.name: Amadou Hott
a189.title: Senegal's former minister of economy and planning and former AfDB vice president, presidential candidate
a189.speech: Called for structural change within the bank to boost its private sector engagement: "What I'm proposing is to convert one of the vice presidencies ... into a vice presidency dedicated to the private sector ... making sure we are more responsive to the private sector and we are mobilizing more resources."

a189.speaker: Sidi Ould Tah, head of the Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa, presidential candidate (Mauritania)
a189.name: Sidi Ould Tah
a189.title: head of the Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa, presidential candidate (Mauritania)
a189.speech: Stressed his track record of institutional reform: "I'm not talking about abstract things. We have been able to multiply approvals by 12 in 10 years ... and to reduce NPL from more than 10% to less than 0.5%." He also proposed a guarantee mechanism to support micro, small, and medium enterprises and boost value-added production on the continent.

a189.speaker: Abbas Mahamat Tolli, governor of the Central Bank of Central African States, presidential candidate (Chad)
a189.name: Abbas Mahamat Tolli
a189.title: governor of the Central Bank of Central African States, presidential candidate (Chad)
a189.speech: Shone a spotlight on the importance of food sovereignty: "We need to work with the member states to make sure that food and agricultural independence becomes a reality." He also called for renewed focus on energy investments and trade-enabling infrastructure ; on internal reform: "It's important to work as a team ... and have also internally a culture that is focused on results, impact, and not just on procedures."

a415.speaker: Reports (cited)
a415.name: Reports (cited)
a415.speech: According to reports, women and youth made up 80 per cent of all beneficiaries.

a945.speaker: Kissi Agyebeng, Special Prosecutor
a945.name: Kissi Agyebeng
a945.title: Special Prosecutor
a945.speech: has defended the bail conditions imposed on broadcaster Paul Adom-Otchere, insisting they are standard and designed to discourage suspects from fleeing the justice process; clarified that all suspects who appear before the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) are required to meet basic legal conditions before being granted bail—one of which is providing landed property as surety ; “The OSP as a suspect—when you say you do not have any landed property, you can't bail yourself if you don't have any landed property” ; explained that while no specific monetary value is placed on the property provided, it serves as a form of insurance that the suspect will appear before investigators or in court when required ; “Bring what you have. It is to encourage you not to run, because if you run away, that property will be confiscated by the state” ; noted that any suspect without landed property effectively becomes a liability on the state and risks having any future assets confiscated if they abscond ; “If you say you don't have anything, you have placed yourself on the state. And anything the state finds on you, it is confiscated. It is as simple as that.”

a945.speaker: Paul Adom-Otchere, former Board Chairman of the Ghana Airports Company Limited (GACL)
a945.name: Paul Adom-Otchere
a945.title: former Board Chairman of the Ghana Airports Company Limited (GACL)
a945.speech: reportedly told investigators that he does not own any landed property in Ghana, prompting his continued detention.

a945.speaker: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP)
a945.name: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP)
a945.speech: has formally charged Paul Adom-Otchere in connection with a controversial revenue assurance contract; is investigating suspected corruption and procurement irregularities surrounding a sole-sourced contract awarded under Mr. Adom-Otchere's watch, a deal which allegedly went to a company other than the one approved by the GACL Board.

a1361.speaker: United Nations (statement/communiqué)
a1361.name: United Nations (statement/communiqué)
a1361.speech: States that these emergency funds aim to "strengthen life-saving assistance in 10 of the world's most underfunded and neglected crises, in Africa, Asia and Latin America", citing in particular Sudan, which is currently facing the world's worst humanitarian crisis ; the funds released today "will also strengthen the humanitarian response in Afghanistan, the Central African Republic, Honduras, Mauritania, Niger, Somalia, Venezuela and Zambia", without giving further details ; adds that by 2025 more than 300 million people will depend on humanitarian aid, "but funding is decreasing every year" and "is expected to fall to a historically low level this year" ; recalls that it estimated humanitarian needs at 45 billion dollars to help 185 million of the most vulnerable people affected by crises around the world, and insists: "To date, only 5% of that funding has been received, leaving a shortfall of more than 42 billion."

a1361.speaker: Tom Fletcher, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator
a1361.name: Tom Fletcher
a1361.title: UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator
a1361.speech: Said: "For countries hit by conflict, climate change and economic crises, drastic budget cuts do not mean that humanitarian needs have disappeared."

a1397.speaker: Prof. Naana Jane Opoku Agyemang, Vice President of Ghana
a1397.name: Prof. Naana Jane Opoku Agyemang
a1397.title: Vice President of Ghana
a1397.speech: Has urged African leaders to strengthen their collaboration in order to realise the vision of a single market. She emphasised that achieving this goal requires unity among industry players, as well as networking towards regional stability. Speaking at the 2025 edition of the Africa Prosperity Dialogue in Accra, she noted that unity, hard work, and networking are essential, but prioritising infrastructure development is equally critical, and that Africa's fragmented markets remain a significant barrier to economic growth. She warned that much of the continent's potential remains untapped due to market division and described integration not just as an abstract concept but as a necessity for Africa's collective future: "By breaking down barriers and creating a single market, we can unlock immense opportunities, create jobs for our youth, and lift millions out of poverty." She described the dialogue's theme as a call to action for resetting and accelerating Africa's journey toward integration and shared benefits.

a1397.speaker: Prof. Naana Jane Opoku Agyemang, Vice President of Ghana (on energy and fintech)
a1397.name: Prof. Naana Jane Opoku Agyemang
a1397.title: Vice President of Ghana (on energy and fintech)
a1397.speech: Commended the progress made in energy infrastructure, highlighting Ghana's investments aimed at ensuring reliable and affordable power for both industries and households. She also addressed the fintech sector, noting that Ghana has prioritised mobile payment interoperability to facilitate trade and promote financial inclusion.

a1397.speaker: Dr. Nkosazana Dlamini Zuma, Chairperson of the African Prosperity Network Advisory Council
a1397.name: Dr. Nkosazana Dlamini Zuma
a1397.title: Chairperson of the African Prosperity Network Advisory Council
a1397.speech: Urged Africans to move beyond merely fitting into the world of work and instead become agents of change at the leadership level. She emphasised the need for Africa to shift from exporting raw natural resources to value addition in order to influence price determination: "Africa is not poor, but its people are, and this should drive the narrative for change and development."

a1397.speaker: Dr Gwen Mwamba, Managing Director of the Africa Export-Import Bank (EXIM)
a1397.name: Dr Gwen Mwamba
a1397.title: Managing Director of the Africa Export-Import Bank (EXIM)
a1397.speech: Called on African leaders to prioritise regional transactions to maximise economic benefits. She noted that enhancing intra-African trade could save the continent an estimated $5 million annually.

a1421.speaker: US Embassy in Nigeria / US Mission to Nigeria (post on X / statement)
a1421.name: US Embassy in Nigeria / US Mission to Nigeria (post on X / statement)
a1421.speech: Has said it probed all assistance given to Nigeria to ensure they reach "intended recipients"; stated that "comprehensive monitoring and evaluation systems are in place to help verify that U.S. assistance reaches intended recipients" ; condemned the "blatant disregard for human life perpetrated by Boko Haram": "The United States condemns the violence and blatant disregard for human life perpetrated by Boko Haram and other terrorist groups in Nigeria and the region," adding that the US Secretary of State designated Boko Haram a Foreign Terrorist Organisation on 14 November 2013 "to block the organisation's assets and fundraising efforts, prosecute individual members and restrict their travel to the United States"; adding that the United States continues to work with Nigeria and regional partners to counter terrorism.

a1421.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman
a1421.name: Scott Perry
a1421.title: US Congressman
a1421.speech: Accused the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) of funding global terrorist groups like Islamic State and al-Qaeda, including their local affiliates such as Boko Haram in Nigeria; during the inaugural session of an advisory body created by Mr Trump to cut US government spending, said the USAID's annual budget of $697 million including cash shipments to madrasas (Islamic schools), has inadvertently funded terrorist training camps and extremist groups.

a1421.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1421.name: Donald Trump
a1421.title: US President
a1421.speech: In January, suspended all foreign aid for 90 days, explaining that the pause was to determine whether the use of those funds aligned with America's interests.

a1421.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES investigation
a1421.name: PREMIUM TIMES investigation
a1421.speech: Some of them were detained for months without trial, according to a PREMIUM TIMES investigation.

a1478.speaker: Ministry of Equipment and Road Maintenance of Côte d'Ivoire (contracting authority of the project)
a1478.name: Ministry of Equipment and Road Maintenance of Côte d'Ivoire (contracting authority of the project)
a1478.speech: did not fail to express its gratitude to the American partner, as well as to the local residents, who demonstrated patience, understanding and great resilience throughout the period of the works.

a1643.speaker: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako, Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.name: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako
a1643.title: Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.speech: Has called for a sustainable financing strategy to champion Ghana's economic reset for transformation. The strategy should create a Ghana development finance platform and comprehensive domestic revenue mobilisation and build long-term agreements with our major external financing partners. Those strategies, the Development Economist said, should be effectively aligned with the country's vision for economic transformation, with a focus on achieving them in the next decade to drive growth and create sustainable jobs for Ghanaians.

a1643.speaker: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako, Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.name: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako
a1643.title: Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.speech: "Ghana's Gross National Income per capita sat stagnant at less than US$400 for almost 40 years, between 1962 and 1999. But since 2000 it has increased to about US$2,400" he said ; "It should not take another 50 years for Ghana to become an upper middle-income country. And I hope that this administration's reset will include raising our ambition. We can, and we must, become a developed economy in the next 20 years," he noted.

a1643.speaker: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako, Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.name: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako
a1643.title: Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.speech: Said the Ghana development finance platform should be used to coordinate the flow of development assistance into the country, assess progress on policy reforms and programmes and ensure that "resources are not duplicative, wasted or misaligned with our development vision."

a1643.speaker: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako, Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.name: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako
a1643.title: Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.speech: Regarding long-term agreements with major external financing partners, he cited the case of Pakistan, where a 10-year agreement with the World Bank has led to the provision of US$20 billion in financial support to the country. Such long-term partnership, he said, was ideal for Ghana's economic reset and transformation, urging the government to explore those avenues.

a1643.speaker: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako, Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.name: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako
a1643.title: Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.speech: Speaking about domestic revenue mobilisation, called for effective strategies to curb illicit financial flows, harness remittances and ensure fair taxation to fuel public services and investments. "The overall goal of this strategy would be to mobilise significantly increased financing coupled with rigorous expenditure management for the next ten years to support our development, underpinned by a strong accountability mechanism."

a1643.speaker: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako, Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.name: Kingsley (K.Y.) Amoako
a1643.title: Member of the National Economic Dialogue Planning Committee and Development Economist
a1643.speech: While applauding President John Dramani Mahama for the dialogue, he recommended that the discussions should focus on concrete policy reforms, institutional strengthening and strategic investments to stabilise the economy, drive growth and create jobs in the medium to long-term.

a1945.speaker: External aid figures (data consulted by the Lusa news agency)
a1945.name: External aid figures (data consulted by the Lusa news agency)
a1945.speech: Reveal that the total value of the aid is in line with the quarterly average of the last nine years and consisted mainly of donations in the form of foreign currency, which accounted for 55% of the total; the remainder corresponded almost entirely to donations of equipment, reaching 663 million escudos in the first three months of the year, with partner Governments delivering around one billion escudos, supranational organisations almost 500 million escudos, NGOs 41 million escudos and private institutions 21 million escudos.

a1945.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance of Cape Verde
a1945.name: Olavo Correia
a1945.title: Minister of Finance of Cape Verde
a1945.speech: Has argued that the country must “begin to learn to live without donations.” ; “We will still need it,” but “they will not remain forever,” as the country develops, he said during the launch of the State Budget (OE) for 2024.

a1962.speaker: Financial Times (statement from London)
a1962.name: Financial Times (statement from London)
a1962.speech: Announces that the 12th edition of its flagship Africa Summit on October 21-22 in London will discuss the continent's role amidst geopolitical and economic uncertainty characterised by the new and second US President Donald Trump's era; indicates that the conference will be held under the theme 'Africa in a Changing World', which will attract African Heads of State, policymakers, CEOs, investors, and next-generation entrepreneurs to explore the continent's global role in a period of geopolitical and economic uncertainty, and technological change.

a1962.speaker: Financial Times (statement from London)
a1962.name: Financial Times (statement from London)
a1962.speech: “The dramatic changes to America’s foreign policy in Donald Trump’s second term and his upending of the decades-old global trading system, present challenges, uncertainties and risks for Africa as other outside powers intervene” ; “The threat to Lesotho’s economy from tariffs underlines the potential peril for some African states — but there are also opportunities for the continent as America prioritises trade and investment over aid.”

a1962.speaker: Financial Times (statement from London)
a1962.name: Financial Times (statement from London)
a1962.speech: Said the high-level speakers lined up include African Union Commission chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf; South Africa's minister of international relations & cooperation Ronald Lamola; Sierra Leone's chief minister & chief innovation officer David Moinina Sengeh; Angola's finance minister Vera Daves de Sousa; Infinity Power chairman Mohamed Mansour and TotalEnergies' Senior Vice-President-Africa Mike Sangster, alongside ministers and business leaders from South Africa, Angola, Nigeria, Egypt, Mauritius, Kenya, and Senegal. It added that the 2025 summit “will examine how African countries are embracing innovation and economic transformation” ; “The summit will also spotlight Africa’s hoped-for transition to renewable energy and also industrial expansion, and the rising influence of youth-led entrepreneurship in shaping sustainable, inclusive growth. The discussions will be facilitated by senior editors from the Financial Times and will feature insight-driven dialogue across geopolitics, tech, energy, infrastructure, trade, investment and finance.” ; “It continues to serve as a valuable forum for conversation and exchange connecting perspectives from across the continent and beyond to help shape the global narrative around Africa’s future.”

a2013.speaker: Authorities of Burkina Faso
a2013.name: Authorities of Burkina Faso
a2013.speech: Claim to have raised territorial reconquest to 72.70% in June 2025, up from 70.89% six months earlier, notably in the Sourou valley as well as at Diapaga and Djibo.

a2013.speaker: Malian army
a2013.name: Malian army
a2013.speech: Announced in July that it had repelled coordinated jihadist attacks against seven strategic localities, neutralising more than 80 JNIM assailants and capturing Abraham Boubacar, alias “Oubel”, a leader of the Islamic State in the Sahel.

a2013.speaker: Global Terrorism Index (report published March 2025)
a2013.name: Global Terrorism Index (report published March 2025)
a2013.speech: Recorded a 94% rise in deaths linked to jihadist violence in Niger in 2024, reaching 930 victims; more broadly, the Sahel alone accounted for 51% of terrorism-related deaths worldwide that same year, with Burkina Faso the worst-affected country for the second consecutive year.

a2237.speaker: Christopher Landau, US Deputy Secretary of State
a2237.name: Christopher Landau
a2237.title: US Deputy Secretary of State
a2237.speech: Said on Wednesday in New York that the American administration "is actively encouraging United States companies to invest in this region of Morocco" ; insisted, during a meeting with Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita, on the role these investments could play in local economic development while consolidating the strategic partnership between Rabat and Washington ; "We are pleased to support American companies wishing to establish themselves in the Southern provinces, as part of an economic diplomacy oriented towards prosperity and regional stability."

a2237.speaker: Christopher Landau, US Deputy Secretary of State
a2237.name: Christopher Landau
a2237.title: US Deputy Secretary of State
a2237.speech: Stressed that the United States remains determined to work alongside Morocco to "promote prosperity, peace and stability in the region."

a2254.speaker: Robert Zantan, Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a2254.name: Robert Zantan
a2254.title: Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a2254.speech: "The signing ceremony reflects the full importance that the Beninese government attaches to the various cooperation activities carried out by the NGO Research Triangle Institute (RTI) for the benefit of the Beninese people, particularly in the field of health, which is one of the priority sectors of the government's national development policy," ; went on to say that RTI's programme of free treatment of neglected tropical diseases - including onchocerciasis or river blindness, lymphatic filariasis or elephantiasis, intestinal worms, schistosomiasis or bilharzia, and trachoma - constitutes tangible proof of this, noting that these diseases wreak great havoc in the shadows ; welcomed RTI's efforts and agreed that RTI should be supported in its activities, whose socio-economic impact no longer needs to be demonstrated, which justified the Beninese government making available to the NGO the premises that house the National Programme for the Fight against Communicable Diseases for administrative and storage needs.

a2254.speaker: Robert Zantan, Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a2254.name: Robert Zantan
a2254.title: Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a2254.speech: Also credited RTI with other programmes geared towards research using a multidisciplinary approach in health and the promotion of the application of scientific and technological innovations in development ; noted that all of this justifies the government granting RTI, through the headquarters agreement, multiple advantages, particularly tax and customs exemptions, and all facilities that can enable it to expand its interventions in the field to improve the well-being of the Beninese people.

a2254.speaker: Robert Zantan, Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a2254.name: Robert Zantan
a2254.title: Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a2254.speech: Did not fail to express his gratitude to the American development aid agency (USAID) for its financial support for the implementation of the "ENVISION" project in Benin.

a2254.speaker: Aboudou Dare, resident adviser of Research Triangle Institute (RTI)
a2254.name: Aboudou Dare
a2254.title: resident adviser of Research Triangle Institute (RTI)
a2254.speech: Welcomed the financial support and the headquarters agreement, convinced that this agreement will further facilitate the NGO's working conditions and will benefit the beneficiaries, who are the populations of the various endemic areas; RTI, with its "ENVISION" project funded by USAID, remains available to support the government in the fight against neglected tropical diseases.

a2254.speaker: Aboudou Dare, resident adviser of Research Triangle Institute (RTI)
a2254.name: Aboudou Dare
a2254.title: resident adviser of Research Triangle Institute (RTI)
a2254.speech: Recalled that for the past two years RTI has been supporting the Ministry of Health through the National Programme for the Fight against Communicable Diseases (PNLMT), support that concerns the fight against neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), including the complete mapping of trachoma and the ongoing mapping of soil-transmitted helminthiases and schistosomiasis, with 38 communes already mapped, the deworming of school-age children (5-14 years) whether in school or not, and the funding of annual reviews of activities against neglected tropical diseases ; took the opportunity to express his gratitude to the partner ministries which all worked towards the signing of this agreement, because for him, "the night has been long but the day has arrived."

a2806.speaker: Clement Kaukuetu, African Aquaculture Company (AAC) Country Director
a2806.name: Clement Kaukuetu
a2806.title: African Aquaculture Company (AAC) Country Director
a2806.speech: "This project is a beacon of opportunity for Namibia. It will not only create jobs but also equip the local population with skills to thrive in the burgeoning global aquaculture industry." ; "With no salmon lice detected in the Benguela Current and meticulous environmental monitoring protocols in place, AAC seeks to meet international certification standards, including Global G.A.P. and Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC) standards."

a2806.speaker: Blue Empire, 2024 NGO report
a2806.name: Blue Empire
a2806.title: 2024 NGO report
a2806.speech: revealed that 2 million tonnes of wild fish are extracted annually to produce feed for farmed salmon, often sourced from food-insecure regions like Northwest Africa.

a2806.speaker: African Aquaculture Company (AAC)
a2806.name: African Aquaculture Company (AAC)
a2806.speech: said it has partnered with Skretting, a Norwegian feed producer committed to transparency in marine ingredient sourcing.

a2806.speaker: UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) data
a2806.name: UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) data
a2806.speech: shows Africa's aquaculture production grew by 12% year-on-year in 2023, though salmon remains a nascent niche.

a2898.speaker: Antonio Guterres, United Nations (UN) chief
a2898.name: Antonio Guterres
a2898.title: United Nations (UN) chief
a2898.speech: Called on Israel to “exercise maximum restraint and respect the right to freedom of peaceful assembly” in occupied East Jerusalem.

a2898.speaker: United States
a2898.name: United States
a2898.speech: Yesterday also expressed “serious concern” of violence in Jerusalem as Israeli police again cracked down on protesters rallying against the forced expulsions of Palestinian families from the occupied East Jerusalem neighbourhood of Sheikh Jarrah.

a2898.speaker: Palestinian Red Crescent
a2898.name: Palestinian Red Crescent
a2898.speech: Said at least 17 people, including one Palestinian paramedic, were wounded during peaceful demonstrations across East Jerusalem on Sunday evening.

a2898.speaker: Penda Naanda, executive director of Namibia's Ministry of International Relations
a2898.name: Penda Naanda
a2898.title: executive director of Namibia's Ministry of International Relations
a2898.speech: Said Namibia expressed concern towards the possible evictions and condemned the violence exercised by the Israeli police during the past days against Palestinian demonstrators and the storming of the al-Aqsa Mosque, assaulting peaceful worshippers. “The government of Namibia expresses its solidarity with the Palestinian people and calls on the Israeli forces to end the violent acts against the Palestinians,” Naanda said.

a2898.speaker: Government of Namibia
a2898.name: Government of Namibia
a2898.speech: Namibia further reaffirmed its resolute support for the legitimate struggle of the Palestinian people against Israeli occupation, the inalienable right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and independence with East Jerusalem as their capital; Namibia calls on the international community to continue supporting the Palestinian people through the implementation of relevant UN resolutions and all other agreements.

a2961.speaker: Abdourahmane Sarr, Senegalese Minister of Economy, Planning and Cooperation
a2961.name: Abdourahmane Sarr
a2961.title: Senegalese Minister of Economy, Planning and Cooperation
a2961.speech: Announced on Saturday the signing of an agreement with the United States under the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), opening the way for a third compact for Senegal centred on the development of the blue economy: “The blue economy is in perfect alignment with the spirit of the new Senegal 2050 framework,” the minister stressed on X (formerly Twitter), explaining that this approach will allow “all components of society to benefit from it through various value chains and infrastructure around coastal cities.”

a2961.speaker: Abdourahmane Sarr, Senegalese Minister of Economy, Planning and Cooperation
a2961.name: Abdourahmane Sarr
a2961.title: Senegalese Minister of Economy, Planning and Cooperation
a2961.speech: Praised the work of the compact formulation unit, headed by Dr. Seydina Sène, which played a decisive role in defining the priority sectors and developing a consensual vision of the blue economy incorporating coastal cities.

a3165.speaker: US Department of the Treasury
a3165.name: US Department of the Treasury
a3165.speech: According to the US Department of the Treasury, the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP) is an initiative aimed at boosting agriculture in 11 African nations; US participation is also a component of President Barack Obama's Feed the Future initiative and represents a unique partnership between donors, partner countries, civil society and multilateral development institutions to scale up financing for agriculture in the poorest countries.

a3165.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock of Burundi
a3165.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock of Burundi
a3165.speech: has identified a series of major problems in the country's agriculture, such as lack of basic ingredients for good farming, small plots, low soil fertility, poor seed quality, and an upsurge in diseases and pests that are destroying key crops such as cassava and bananas, and diseases in livestock.

a3165.speaker: Representatives of the US Embassy in Bujumbura
a3165.name: Representatives of the US Embassy in Bujumbura
a3165.speech: said Tuesday that answers to questions from Burundi will be provided soon.

a3356.speaker: Korir Sing'oei, Principal Secretary of Kenya's Foreign Ministry
a3356.name: Korir Sing'oei
a3356.title: Principal Secretary of Kenya's Foreign Ministry
a3356.speech: Said Kenya is working to transition its Haiti security mission into a UN operation following a disruption in US funding, and that despite a 90-day US hold on funds the mission on the Caribbean island remains operational with existing resources; emphasized that the US has committed approximately $600 million to the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission, with a significant portion already disbursed: "The only thing the US has done is to say, okay, let's pause further disbursement to the trust fund for 90 days. That only affects about $15 million. The mission already has $110 million to continue operations, and we are very confident that other countries will come on board." ; "It cannot be stopped in terms of being used, because it's money already disbursed."

a3356.speaker: Korir Sing'oei, Principal Secretary of Kenya's Foreign Ministry
a3356.name: Korir Sing'oei
a3356.title: Principal Secretary of Kenya's Foreign Ministry
a3356.speech: Said there are plans to transition the mission to a UN operation, which would enable access to contributions directly from UN statutory funds: "The reality also is that this mission will be transitioned to a UN mission, which will enable it to assess contributions directly from the UN statutory funds." ; "So Kenya's stand is that the mission will still go ahead," he reaffirmed, dismissing concerns that the U.S. funding pause would derail deployment efforts.

a3371.speaker: Community leaders of the Somali community in Eldoret
a3371.name: Community leaders of the Somali community in Eldoret
a3371.speech: Briefed the Ambassador on challenges they face, particularly in travel and trade, and agreed to establish a committee for continuous liaison with the Embassy.

a3371.speaker: Jabril Ibrahim Abdulle, Somali Ambassador to Kenya
a3371.name: Jabril Ibrahim Abdulle
a3371.title: Somali Ambassador to Kenya
a3371.speech: Thanked local leaders and residents for their warm reception, noting the progress of the Somali government and the positive relations between Kenya and Somalia.

a3396.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3396.name: Badr Abdelatty
a3396.title: Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3396.speech: Expressed, jointly with his Iranian counterpart, condemnation of the persistent violence targeting Palestinian civilians, and detailed the efforts being led by Egypt to halt the Israeli attacks and to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip; he also offered his condolences to Iran following the incident that occurred at the port of Shahid Rajaei, wishing a speedy recovery to the injured.

a3396.speaker: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3396.name: Seyed Abbas Araghchi
a3396.title: Iranian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3396.speech: Denounced the blockade imposed on Gaza as well as the civilian losses, which he described as unprecedented crimes; he accused the United States and Israel's allies of complicity in what he described as genocide; he also warned against the forced displacement of Palestinians and criticised the inaction of the international community; finally, he informed Abdelatty of the latest developments in the indirect negotiations between Tehran and Washington.

a3406.speaker: Adellaide Migogo, Chairperson of the National Women's Football Association (NWFA)
a3406.name: Adellaide Migogo
a3406.title: Chairperson of the National Women's Football Association (NWFA)
a3406.speech: Has challenged Malawi Women's National Football Team players to use the absence of the Chawinga sisters, Tabitha and Temwa, as their stepping stone to greatness; said the absence of the seven was a blessing in disguise as it had given other players a chance to shine and help the country defend the championship: "Much as we would have loved to have the seven to be part of the squad but circumstances did not allow. Nevertheless, it is their chance to shine and help the country retain the cup. Our squad is full of quality and I believe other players will step up to fill the void left by the absence of the seven. This is where they have to fight to market themselves to earn lucrative deals."

a3406.speaker: Adellaide Migogo, Chairperson of the National Women's Football Association (NWFA)
a3406.name: Adellaide Migogo
a3406.title: Chairperson of the National Women's Football Association (NWFA)
a3406.speech: Said the Scorchers' performance since 2022 has been improving and retaining the cup was their ultimate mission: "In 2022 the Scorchers lost in the final and a year later they won. We have to work hard to defend the cup this time around."

a3406.speaker: Patricia Nyirenda, Scorchers squad captain
a3406.name: Patricia Nyirenda
a3406.title: Scorchers squad captain
a3406.speech: Said they were geared to put extra effort to defend the cup: "We are the Scorchers and a lot is expected from us. We will try our best to defend the cup so that our compatriots should be happy too."

a3442.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (press statement / communiqué)
a3442.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (press statement / communiqué)
a3442.speech: Expressed its surprise following the publication by the United States Department of Government Efficiency on 15 February 2025 concerning US$14 million in aid — nearly nine billion CFA francs — provided by USAID "in support of social cohesion in Mali"; underlined that for two years, on grounds of sovereignty and security, the government has refrained from signing the five-year Development Objective Grant Agreement with the United States, worth more than $631.66 million (about 400 billion CFA francs), relating to USAID funding, and specified that the US Embassy in Mali is fully aware of Mali's reservations; stated that the Transition government's position stems on the one hand from the will of Malians expressed at the National Consultations on Refoundation (ANR) to rebuild their country, and on the other from the determination of the highest authorities to eradicate terrorism.

a3442.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (press statement / communiqué)
a3442.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (press statement / communiqué)
a3442.speech: Stated that the Head of State has come to the conclusion that certain forms of aid, in addition to undermining State sovereignty, constitute means of financing international terrorism; said that following the recent denunciations by the American authorities concerning the misappropriation of USAID funds for various purposes, notably the financing and support of terrorism, the Transition government welcomes this new orientation and invites them to initiate legal proceedings against those guilty of financing international terrorism, of which Mali and the other States of the AES Confederation are victims; invited the American authorities to provide it with fuller information on the alleged $14 million in USAID aid "in support of social cohesion in Mali," all the more so as the five-year Development Objective Grant Agreement with the United States has still not been signed by Mali; and thanked the US Embassy in Bamako for its good collaboration, renewing the assurances of its highest consideration.

a3442.speaker: United States Department of Government Efficiency (publication of 15 February 2025)
a3442.name: United States Department of Government Efficiency (publication of 15 February 2025)
a3442.speech: Published information concerning US$14 million in aid provided by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) "in support of social cohesion in Mali"; the American authorities also recently denounced cases of misappropriation of USAID funds for various purposes, notably the financing and support of terrorism.

a3554.speaker: Norwegian Embassy in Juba (press statement)
a3554.name: Norwegian Embassy in Juba (press statement)
a3554.speech: Announced an additional contribution of 140 million Norwegian Kroner ($12.6 million) to address urgent food security and protection needs among vulnerable communities in South Sudan; said the initiative seeks to alleviate acute food shortages worsened by conflict, climate change, and economic instability.

a3554.speaker: Norwegian Embassy in Juba (the Mission)
a3554.name: Norwegian Embassy in Juba (the Mission)
a3554.speech: Said that by addressing the root causes of hunger and promoting local agricultural production, South Sudan can pave the way for a self-reliant country; reiterated Norway’s steadfast commitment in assisting South Sudan’s development programs – having contributed over $100 million in the past year.

a3554.speaker: Roar Haugsdal, Norwegian Ambassador to South Sudan
a3554.name: Roar Haugsdal
a3554.title: Norwegian Ambassador to South Sudan
a3554.speech: “Food insecurity remains one of the most pressing challenges in South Sudan, with millions facing hunger daily.” ; “It is vital that the people, government, and international donors work together to create long-term solutions to reduce hunger and food insecurity.”

a3554.speaker: Roar Haugsdal, Norwegian Ambassador to South Sudan
a3554.name: Roar Haugsdal
a3554.title: Norwegian Ambassador to South Sudan
a3554.speech: Called on South Sudanese leaders to demonstrate political will by implementing the extended 2018 peace accord known as the R-ARCSS and making meaningful compromises during the Tumaini peace talks.

a3554.speaker: United Nations (estimates)
a3554.name: United Nations (estimates)
a3554.speech: Estimates that approximately 9 million people in South Sudan required urgent humanitarian assistance in 2024, with food insecurity reaching critical levels in many areas.

a3557.speaker: Technical Unit for Monitoring and Support of Food Security Management (Ct/Sagsa), Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries (monthly agricultural market bulletin)
a3557.name: Technical Unit for Monitoring and Support of Food Security Management (Ct/Sagsa)
a3557.title: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries (monthly agricultural market bulletin)
a3557.speech: Reported that in November 2023 a slight fall in prices (-5%) month-on-month was observed for local rice, at 498 CFA francs per kilogram, indicating surges of 6% and 17% year-on-year and against the five-year average; revealed that these surges would be due to an increase in demand for local rice following the rise in the price of imported rice, linked to India’s current policy on exports of non-basmati white rice ; “Based on the typology of markets, a fall in prices was observed on assembly markets (-4%), border markets (-7%) and producer markets (-6%) compared with the previous month. However, an increase is noted on consumer markets (+4%).”

a3609.speaker: Organizers of the conference (National Authority for the Fight against Corruption, ANLC)
a3609.name: Organizers of the conference (National Authority for the Fight against Corruption
a3609.title: ANLC)
a3609.speech: According to the organizers, the overall objective of this conference is to prompt broader reflection among the actors involved in the fight against transnational organized crime and corruption in Benin with a view to energizing the fight against these two phenomena — specifically, sharing with participants the content of the special study on Transnational Organized Crime (TOC) and corruption, in particular its arms-trafficking aspect; sharing the content of the second quarterly assessment of judicial proceedings relating to TOC and corruption cases; sharing the cross-cutting experience of professionals in the fight against transnational organized crime in Benin at the institutional and jurisdictional levels; and gathering recommendations for a more effective fight against corruption and transnational organized crime.

a3609.speaker: Guy Ogoubiyi, President of the National Authority for the Fight against Corruption (ANLC), Benin
a3609.name: Guy Ogoubiyi
a3609.title: President of the National Authority for the Fight against Corruption (ANLC), Benin
a3609.speech: In his remarks at the opening of the proceedings, first recalled the “Ayifa” project which, he said, falls within the framework of Benin’s West African Security Cooperation Initiative Program launched by the government. He underlined that the conjunction of transnational organized crime (TOC) and corruption and arms trafficking linked to gang robberies in Benin calls for reflection in view of the security situation in the West African sub-region in general and Benin’s geographic position in particular. He also expressed the wish that the recommendations be of high quality in order to improve the institutional and regulatory framework needed to begin rolling back transnational organized crime and corruption in Benin.

a3609.speaker: Yikee Chu Adjé, representative of USAID-Benin
a3609.name: Yikee Chu Adjé
a3609.title: representative of USAID-Benin
a3609.speech: spoke about the importance of the theme, which she described as topical; it is a worrying phenomenon that deserves an appropriate response and the support of the international community. “The phenomenon deserves sustained attention from the government and requires a global reflection on the situation in order to assess the institutional framework in place and counter the phenomenon,” she notes. “The security of citizens and of economic activities is a guarantee of development,” she concluded.

a3716.speaker: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a3716.name: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a3716.speech: According to the ICRC, International Humanitarian Law “protects persons who are no longer participating in hostilities and restricts the means and methods of warfare.”

a3716.speaker: ‘Mabataung Khalane, Principal Secretary, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Office (opening remarks)
a3716.name: ‘Mabataung Khalane
a3716.title: Principal Secretary, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Office (opening remarks)
a3716.speech: Emphasized Lesotho’s dedication to IHL, stating: “The Government of Lesotho understands that IHL applies only in armed conflict, offering two systems of protection – one for international conflicts and another for non-international conflicts. It strikes a balance between humanity and military necessity.” ; highlighted key IHL principles that focus on distinction, protection and compliance, saying parties in conflict must differentiate between civilians and combatants and that Lesotho recognizes the binding nature of these IHL instruments and customary law ; said the project underscores Lesotho’s commitment to strengthening legal frameworks for conflict mitigation, enhancing humanitarian diplomacy through cross-sector collaboration and promoting accountability in warfare to protect vulnerable populations ; described customary law as formed when “state practice is sufficiently dense – widespread, representative, frequent and uniform – and accompanied by a belief among states that they are legally bound to act – or prohibited from acting – in certain ways.”

a3716.speaker: Sarah Mabeza, Regional Legal Advisor of the Pretoria Delegation of the ICRC
a3716.name: Sarah Mabeza
a3716.title: Regional Legal Advisor of the Pretoria Delegation of the ICRC
a3716.speech: Stated that ICRC is a neutral, impartial and independent entity that is able to reach those in need when others cannot, and said this is done through providing humanitarian assistance, protecting lives, upholding rights and relieving the suffering of people around the world whose lives have been torn apart by armed conflict and violence ; pointed out that the ICRC is operational in 90 countries across the globe, that over 90 percent of donations received go directly to the field, and that ICRC is the oldest organisation in the world with a lifespan of 160 years ; “Humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity and universality: these are fundamental principles that guide and define not only our work, but also the work of National Red Cross Societies worldwide, including the LRCS.” ; stressed that the ICRC operates in accordance with the principles of IHL based on the Geneva Conventions of 1949, their Additional Protocols, the Statutes of the international Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and the resolutions of the international Conferences of the Red Cross and Red Crescent ; “We take action to assist the victims of armed conflict and other violence, and at the same time promote respect for the IHL and implementation in domestic law.”

a3761.speaker: Official source (anonymous)
a3761.name: Official source (anonymous)
a3761.speech: Disclosed today that the Prime Minister will head the country's delegation to the China-Africa Cooperation Forum next week, where he intends to map out new areas of cooperation.

a3761.speaker: Alexandre Monteiro, Cabo Verdean Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy
a3761.name: Alexandre Monteiro
a3761.title: Cabo Verdean Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy
a3761.speech: Said today that in buying electric vehicles in Cabo Verde interested parties may obtain discounts of more than 600 contos, in addition to tax incentives.

a3886.speaker: Colonel-Major Bana Alhassane, Governor of the Dosso Region
a3886.name: Colonel-Major Bana Alhassane
a3886.title: Governor of the Dosso Region
a3886.speech: In his launch speech, said that the construction of these works forms part of the implementation of PIDUREM, whose objective is to increase resilience to flooding and improve urban management and access to basic services. ; Recalled the damage caused by the heavy rains of 2024, with more than 1,400,000 victims nationwide, of whom the Dosso region recorded more than 220,000 victims and, unfortunately, 25 deaths. ; "The present ceremony is the concretisation of a project of great strategic importance for the urban commune of Dosso and expresses the concrete commitment of the highest authorities, first among them the President of the Republic, Head of State, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani."

a3886.speaker: Colonel-Major Bana Alhassane, Governor of the Dosso Region
a3886.name: Colonel-Major Bana Alhassane
a3886.title: Governor of the Dosso Region
a3886.speech: Invited the beneficiary populations to peacefully vacate the spaces dedicated to the construction of these infrastructures in order to facilitate the work of the contracting company, and asked them to pay particular attention to the maintenance of the infrastructure that will be built.

a3886.speaker: Colonel-Major Bana Alhassane, Governor of the Dosso Region
a3886.name: Colonel-Major Bana Alhassane
a3886.title: Governor of the Dosso Region
a3886.speech: On behalf of the highest authorities, thanked the technical and financial partners, particularly the World Bank, for its constant cooperation and support in the noble and permanent struggle to improve the living conditions of the Nigerien population.

a3886.speaker: Adarkas Oumarou, Regional Coordinator of PIDUREM Dosso
a3886.name: Adarkas Oumarou
a3886.title: Regional Coordinator of PIDUREM Dosso
a3886.speech: Gave a summary presentation of the Project, which officially began its activities on 1 November 2022 for a duration of 6 years with a total cost of 252 million US dollars, or approximately 140 billion CFA francs; said the project will be implemented in 25 municipalities of Niger, three of them in the Dosso region, and that several activities programmed in the 2025 annual work plan and budget are under way in all the project's intervention areas.

a3886.speaker: Ibrahim Moussa Koure, Mayor of the urban commune of Dosso
a3886.name: Ibrahim Moussa Koure
a3886.title: Mayor of the urban commune of Dosso
a3886.speech: In his welcome speech, thanked PIDUREM, especially its regional coordination unit which stands alongside the commune in order to give it the image of a more beautiful and above all more attractive city.

a3983.speaker: Officials present at the ceremony (MENFOP and FHI 360 representatives)
a3983.name: Officials present at the ceremony (MENFOP and FHI 360 representatives)
a3983.speech: In their remarks, the personalities present each in turn stressed the importance and value of the assessment, which they specified makes it possible to measure pupils’ levels and to situate the quality level of the Djiboutian education system relative to those of other countries of the world.

a4104.speaker: Julius Debrah, Chief of Staff at the Presidency of Ghana
a4104.name: Julius Debrah
a4104.title: Chief of Staff at the Presidency of Ghana
a4104.speech: Called on newly appointed envoys to become passionate ambassadors of Ghana’s rich heritage, locally made products and vibrant culture, emphasizing that representing Ghana goes beyond diplomacy and protocol: “Don’t just carry the flag; carry the story of our chocolate, our textiles, our shea butter, our beads, our stools and our crafts because behind each product is a piece of Ghana’s soul.” ; urged the envoys to be intentional about showcasing Ghanaian products and to “master the stories” behind them: “As you have been posted to another country, let someone in that country get to know about Ghanaian chocolate, not just as a product, but as a story of Ghanaian cocoa farmers, our unique processing and the taste of authenticity.” ; “When you speak about kente, speak about its origins, the meanings in the patterns and how it represents unity and pride.”

a4104.speaker: Julius Debrah, Chief of Staff at the Presidency of Ghana
a4104.name: Julius Debrah
a4104.title: Chief of Staff at the Presidency of Ghana
a4104.speech: Recalled a recent interaction at the Presidency where an American visitor brought a traditional stool and kente cloth, claiming it brought positive energy into his home: “That’s the power of our culture. We must take ownership of it and market it proudly just like the American.”

a4104.speaker: Julius Debrah, Chief of Staff at the Presidency of Ghana
a4104.name: Julius Debrah
a4104.title: Chief of Staff at the Presidency of Ghana
a4104.speech: Called for deeper collaboration between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and the private sector to create stronger channels for the export and visibility of Made-in-Ghana products: “We cannot keep importing what we can produce. If we do not champion our own, no one else will.”

a4113.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) press release
a4113.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) press release
a4113.speech: “the members of the Board of Directors considered the fact that these two countries (Benin and Sierra Leone, Ed.) did not obtain a passing score on the indicator relating to corruption,” an MCC press release stated.

a4113.speaker: Daniel W. Yohannes, Chairman of the MCC Board of Directors
a4113.name: Daniel W. Yohannes
a4113.title: Chairman of the MCC Board of Directors
a4113.speech: “We are very concerned when a country fails the corruption indicator. We recognize the efforts that the governments of Benin and Sierra Leone have made in the fight against corruption, and I can assure them that the MCC is committed to helping them so that those efforts succeed. I am hopeful that the two countries’ continued and deepened efforts will be taken into account in future performance on the control of corruption indicator.”

a4382.speaker: Leonardo Santos Simão, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS)
a4382.name: Leonardo Santos Simão
a4382.title: Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS)
a4382.speech: Congratulated the people of Ghana on the success of the presidential and parliamentary elections of 7 December 2024, marked by peace and order ; underlined the exemplary responsibility of the stakeholders and the commitment of the candidates and political leaders to preserving peace throughout the electoral process, which, he said, represents important progress in consolidating Ghana’s democratic gains ; described the country as a “model of political maturity and pragmatism” ; welcomed the “exemplary and gracious concession” of Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, calling on him to unite behind the president-elect, John Dramani Mahama ; added that Ghana continues to serve as an example for the rise of democracy in Africa.

a4382.speaker: United Nations
a4382.name: United Nations
a4382.speech: In partnership with regional actors, reaffirmed its support for the people of Ghana in their quest for democratic consolidation and prosperity.

a4382.speaker: Jean Mensah, Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of Ghana
a4382.name: Jean Mensah
a4382.title: Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of Ghana
a4382.speech: On Monday evening declared John Dramani Mahama the winner of the 2024 presidential election.

a4382.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President-elect of Ghana and leader of the National Democratic Congress (NDC)
a4382.name: John Dramani Mahama
a4382.title: President-elect of Ghana and leader of the National Democratic Congress (NDC)
a4382.speech: In a statement, hailed this victory as a decisive turning point for the country ; expressed his gratitude to the outgoing vice-president, Mahamudu Bawumia, for having conceded defeat before the official announcement, thereby helping to ease tensions ; expressed his desire to ensure a “smooth” transition for the good of the Ghanaian people ; describing his victory as “resounding”, stressed that he had received a clear mandate from the voters: “The support we received is one of the most significant in the history of the Fourth Republic” ; paid tribute to his running mate, Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang: “You have opened the way for many women, here and elsewhere. Today, we are celebrating a historic step forward” ; promised reforms: “We must restore trust between the leaders and the people. Ghana must once again become the Black Star of Africa,” calling on his compatriots to transform “our anger into positive energy to rebuild our nation.”

a4382.speaker: Nana Akufo-Addo, outgoing President of Ghana
a4382.name: Nana Akufo-Addo
a4382.title: outgoing President of Ghana
a4382.speech: Congratulated his successor by telephone, and the two agreed on the establishment of a transition team as of Wednesday 11 December.

a4382.speaker: United States Embassy (Ghana)
a4382.name: United States Embassy (Ghana)
a4382.speech: Congratulated Ghana on having organised “an exemplary election” and expressed its willingness to work with the new government.

a4382.speaker: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a4382.name: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a4382.speech: Also welcomed the peaceful transition and Bawumia’s acknowledgement of defeat, describing it as “honourable.”

a4382.speaker: Police authorities (Ghana)
a4382.name: Police authorities (Ghana)
a4382.speech: According to police authorities, despite the peaceful conduct of the vote, isolated incidents were reported, causing casualties in the north and the central region of the country.

a4453.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a4453.name: Donald Trump
a4453.title: US President-elect
a4453.speech: Posted on Truth Social an image of Joe Biden in front of a board describing the five points of his economic policy: "You pay taxes"; "I send them to Ukraine"; "They send them back to Hunter"; "Hunter gives them to me"; "I pardon Hunter."

a4453.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a4453.name: Donald Trump
a4453.title: US President-elect
a4453.speech: Had already described the decision to pardon Hunter Biden as "an abuse and a miscarriage of justice."

a4496.speaker: Dr Patrick Kiiti Mutuo, Country Representative of the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA)
a4496.name: Dr Patrick Kiiti Mutuo
a4496.title: Country Representative of the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA)
a4496.speech: Announced the results achieved: "The AID-I GLR project, known as the Kugwiza Project, is being implemented by partner organisations in 34 communes spread across 11 provinces." "Out of 504,048 targeted farmers and livestock keepers, 470,000 have been reached from January 2023 to the end of March 2024."

a4496.speaker: Dr Patrick Kiiti Mutuo, Country Representative of the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA)
a4496.name: Dr Patrick Kiiti Mutuo
a4496.title: Country Representative of the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA)
a4496.speech: Reported at the press conference that the AID-I GLR project also introduced licking blocks for animal feed, manufactured from local products to make them accessible to livestock keepers and to reduce the purchase cost, and added that Kugwiza introduced at least 3 new varieties of orange-fleshed sweet potato (Naspot 12 & 9, Yanzovu) of nutritional importance, particularly for children and breastfeeding women, as a source of vitamins: "They can be used in the processing/manufacture of bread and doughnuts by bakers." ; Said that, in collaboration with Seed System Group (SSG), the project introduced and disseminated two hybrid maize varieties (Bazooka & Wannak) as well as silos for storing cereals, particularly maize and beans, and that to improve animal health cows and calves were respectively inseminated and vaccinated against theileriosis (Umupfube).

a4496.speaker: Théodore Riziki, agronomist implementing the Kugwiza project in Muyinga on behalf of World Vision
a4496.name: Théodore Riziki
a4496.title: agronomist implementing the Kugwiza project in Muyinga on behalf of World Vision
a4496.speech: "The project makes it easier for people to obtain selected, certified and high-yielding seed," he said with delight; according to him, the project builds capacity in good agricultural practices and raises awareness about using recommended agricultural inputs, particularly certified seed suited to their land.

a4496.speaker: Serge Sayukubara, president of the "Rugari tugwize imbuto" cooperative
a4496.name: Serge Sayukubara
a4496.title: president of the "Rugari tugwize imbuto" cooperative
a4496.speech: Believes the bean field that used to yield at most 2.5 tonnes will yield 4 tonnes thanks to the good agricultural practices learned; according to him, no one in the neighbourhood will have a bean harvest as good as his cooperative's, which is why people are beginning to contact him to find out where he obtained the seed; he added that the seller of the variety and the seed will be available from the same supplier during the next season, in October.

a4496.speaker: Consesa Ntakarutimana, member of the "Rugari tugwize imbuto" cooperative
a4496.name: Consesa Ntakarutimana
a4496.title: member of the "Rugari tugwize imbuto" cooperative
a4496.speech: Indicates that the benefit of the information provided under the Kugwiza project is great, because previously she farmed any old way without following modern methods of respecting rows and the spacing between plants; she says she experimented herself by planting the selected seed and is committed to buying seed from seed producers every growing season.

a4496.speaker: Marc Nyabenda, member of the Tugwize umwimbu mu bworozi cooperative (Mwurire hill, Muyinga)
a4496.name: Marc Nyabenda
a4496.title: member of the Tugwize umwimbu mu bworozi cooperative (Mwurire hill, Muyinga)
a4496.speech: "The cows have increased milk production from 2 l/day to 7 l/day. The purchase cost of the blocks has fallen from 25,000 Fbu to 11,000 Fbu." He said the licking block contains the nutrients his cows need ; "My cow gives 4 l of milk a day, whereas before it did not exceed two litres."

a4496.speaker: Philibert Sinzinkayo, member of the licking-block cooperative
a4496.name: Philibert Sinzinkayo
a4496.title: member of the licking-block cooperative
a4496.speech: Indicates that since October 2023 at least 104 licking blocks have been made, of which 55 were sold; he says a cow that licks a block has a big appetite and drinks a lot of water, so it produces a lot of milk.

a4496.speaker: Mariette Ntirampeba, president of the sweet potato cooperative
a4496.name: Mariette Ntirampeba
a4496.title: president of the sweet potato cooperative
a4496.speech: On 1.5 ha, expects a harvest of at least 10 tonnes whereas the same land could not produce more than 4 sacks of sweet potato; she is pleased that her cooperative supplied the Rugari secondary school with sweet potato twice.

a4496.speaker: Members of the Nguvuzumukenyezimwiterambere rice cooperative (Nyanza marshland, Ngozi)
a4496.name: Members of the Nguvuzumukenyezimwiterambere rice cooperative (Nyanza marshland
a4496.title: Ngozi)
a4496.speech: Confirmed having received training in rice cultivation, the development and management of irrigation plots, sowing, fertilisation and the control of diseases and pests; the beneficiaries testify to the increase in their yields, rising from 4 to 5 tonnes per hectare.

a4496.speaker: Jeanne Uwurukundo, president of the Nguvuzumukenyezimwiterambere cooperative
a4496.name: Jeanne Uwurukundo
a4496.title: president of the Nguvuzumukenyezimwiterambere cooperative
a4496.speech: "The project introduced 5 varieties to test their adaptation, and two varieties, V564 and L662, were selected for their good yield." ; "Before, we farmed in a disorganised way, we used a lot of seed without mineral fertiliser. Now we know how to set up nurseries for germination, the system of transplanting in rows, and harvesting techniques." ; She invites other rice growers to adopt these new varieties and calls on the Kugwiza project to help the cooperative become a certified rice seed multiplier.

a4496.speaker: Members of the Rematwitezimbere cooperative (Nyangungu hill, Mutaho)
a4496.name: Members of the Rematwitezimbere cooperative (Nyangungu hill
a4496.title: Mutaho)
a4496.speech: Acknowledge that the project has brought a particular change to their farming practices: "They taught us to farm in a modern way on a demonstration plot."

a4496.speaker: Viviane Nzirubusa, member of the Rematwitezimbere cooperative
a4496.name: Viviane Nzirubusa
a4496.title: member of the Rematwitezimbere cooperative
a4496.speech: "They gave us 100 g to go and try at home. At harvest, we were astonished to see 4 tonnes"; according to her, what she tried on a small plot yielded 14 kg of maize.

a4496.speaker: Baltazar Nshimirimana, beneficiary responsible for a demonstration plot
a4496.name: Baltazar Nshimirimana
a4496.title: beneficiary responsible for a demonstration plot
a4496.speech: Affirmed that on 1/4 ha the harvest of Bazooka maize was one tonne, whereas before, on the same land, he obtained about 200 kg with the local Isega variety.

a4496.speaker: Silo beneficiaries
a4496.name: Silo beneficiaries
a4496.speech: Recount that this equipment can preserve the harvest for more than 4 years.

a4496.speaker: Isaac Hakizimana, livestock keeper from Mugitega hill, Bugendana commune
a4496.name: Isaac Hakizimana
a4496.title: livestock keeper from Mugitega hill, Bugendana commune
a4496.speech: Welcomes the project, thanks to which his calves were vaccinated: "The project came at just the right time, because I had lost two calves to theileriosis," he testified.

a4496.speaker: Christophe Gagungu, head of implementation of the Kugwiza project
a4496.name: Christophe Gagungu
a4496.title: head of implementation of the Kugwiza project
a4496.speech: Said the project works with local partners and national seed systems by drawing on the expertise of World Vision, ACORD, Welthungerhilfe (WHH), Vétérinaires sans frontières (VSF), the World Food Programme (WFP), CAPAD and One Acre Fund (OAF-Tubura); he says he is satisfied with the results achieved in transferring innovations and technologies and sincerely thanks the implementing partners as well as the farmers and livestock keepers.

a4496.speaker: International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA)
a4496.name: International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA)
a4496.speech: Is pleased with the dissemination of innovations and technologies on good agricultural and livestock practices to 470,000 beneficiaries out of 504,048 beneficiaries planned in the 34 communes of the 11 provinces of intervention.

a4589.speaker: Gerson Msigwa, Government Chief Spokesperson and Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Information, Culture, Arts and Sports (Tanzania)
a4589.name: Gerson Msigwa
a4589.title: Government Chief Spokesperson and Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Information, Culture, Arts and Sports (Tanzania)
a4589.speech: Assured the public that there is a sufficient reserve of ARVs and clear arrangements to maintain their provision to those in need: "We have made preparations to ensure that those who rely on ARV continue to receive them. In case of any disruptions in the supply chain, the government will ensure continued free distribution." He noted that the current ARV stock is sufficient for the next five months.

a4589.speaker: Ministry of Health of Tanzania (statement)
a4589.name: Ministry of Health of Tanzania (statement)
a4589.speech: Released a statement on Saturday reiterating the government's commitment to ensuring continued access to ARV, and urged people living with HIV to remain calm and adhere to their medication as prescribed by health professionals for effective treatment.

a4589.speaker: Analysts and academics
a4589.name: Analysts and academics
a4589.speech: Advised the Tanzanian government to explore alternative funding sources to sustain social and economic services previously supported by aid agencies, stressing the need for the government to prioritise self-reliance and emphasising that foreign aid is unpredictable and should not be a long-term solution.

a4589.speaker: Dr Isaac Safari, economist at Saint Augustine University of Tanzania (SAUT)
a4589.name: Dr Isaac Safari
a4589.title: economist at Saint Augustine University of Tanzania (SAUT)
a4589.speech: Stated that the US decision to halt aid programmes in Africa, including Tanzania, is a wake-up call for African leaders to maximise their countries' resources rather than depending on foreign donors: "It is wrong to continue believing that the US will always be there to support us. Moving forward, we must use the experience gained from their support to finance development projects across sectors using our own resources" ; "The challenges we face today are within our power to resolve. We must generate our own funds for essential services like medicine by working hard and making the most of our resources." He expressed optimism that Africa's problems can be addressed effectively if Africans maximise the use of their natural and financial resources.

a4589.speaker: Professor Humphrey Moshi, economist and founding director of the Centre for Chinese Studies at the University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM)
a4589.name: Professor Humphrey Moshi
a4589.title: economist and founding director of the Centre for Chinese Studies at the University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM)
a4589.speech: Advised developing countries like Tanzania to seek partnerships with other nations, such as China, while simultaneously working towards self-sufficiency; echoed the sentiment that true national development cannot rely solely on foreign aid.

a4589.speaker: Professor Anna Tibaijuka, former UN Executive Director for Habitat and former Minister for Lands
a4589.name: Professor Anna Tibaijuka
a4589.title: former UN Executive Director for Habitat and former Minister for Lands
a4589.speech: Recently voiced concerns via her X (formerly Twitter) account about the potential negative impact of halting the Global Fund and the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) on Tanzania's healthcare sector, and called for urgent intervention to prevent a crisis; warned that suspending these aid programmes could severely disrupt ARV availability for people living with HIV; also cautioned that the cost of purchasing ARVs is likely to rise, warning of a potential supply gap due to inadequate funding in least developed countries like Tanzania.

a4589.speaker: Professor Anna Tibaijuka, former UN Executive Director for Habitat and former Minister for Lands
a4589.name: Professor Anna Tibaijuka
a4589.title: former UN Executive Director for Habitat and former Minister for Lands
a4589.speech: Urged the African Union to convene a special summit to discuss the issue and formulate a collective response to the crisis, emphasising that a significant number of people living with HIV are in Africa, making it imperative for African leaders to unite in the fight against the disease: "Let us protect ourselves. Efforts to end HIV must be renewed, as the availability of ARVs will become increasingly challenging in the future" ; "This issue has become an emergency, as many people living with HIV lack the financial means to afford ARVs for a lifetime."

a4589.speaker: US Embassy in Tanzania (published data/report)
a4589.name: US Embassy in Tanzania (published data/report)
a4589.speech: According to data published by the US Embassy in Tanzania, PEPFAR has played a crucial role in reducing AIDS related deaths by almost 80 per cent since 2003 and lowering new infections by nearly 60 per cent; the report highlights that when the programme began, fewer than 1,000 Tanzanians were on HIV treatment, while today more than 1.5 million people in the country are receiving life-saving treatment through PEPFAR.

a4589.speaker: Elibariki Kingu, Chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and HIV/AIDS (Tanzania)
a4589.name: Elibariki Kingu
a4589.title: Chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and HIV/AIDS (Tanzania)
a4589.speech: Speaking in the National Assembly last Tuesday, raised concerns about the rising number of HIV cases among young people aged 15 to 24 years; called on the government to increase awareness campaigns targeting youth to prevent new infections, and urged the government to allocate sufficient funding for HIV prevention and treatment programmes to curb the spread of the disease.

a4589.speaker: Trump administration
a4589.name: Trump administration
a4589.speech: Has confirmed plans to merge USAID into the State Department in a major restructuring effort that would reduce its workforce and align spending with Trump's policy priorities.

a4589.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a4589.name: Marco Rubio
a4589.title: US Secretary of State
a4589.speech: Confirmed on Monday that he is now the acting head of USAID amid growing public speculation about the future of the foreign aid organisation; speaking to reporters in El Salvador, Rubio stated that he is overseeing the agency, referring to himself as its acting director.

a4645.speaker: TikTok (company statement)
a4645.name: TikTok (company statement)
a4645.speech: said in a statement that the ban “would trample the free speech rights.”

a4645.speaker: A survey conducted in 2023
a4645.name: A survey conducted in 2023
a4645.speech: revealed that over three-quarters of Generation Z are using TikTok.

a4645.speaker: The TikTok divestment bill (US legislation)
a4645.name: The TikTok divestment bill (US legislation)
a4645.speech: According to the bill, this legislation will assist the U.S. government in identifying foreign applications that “pose a national security threat” to the U.S.

a4666.speaker: United Nations (UN), citing local authorities
a4666.name: United Nations (UN)
a4666.title: citing local authorities
a4666.speech: Said late Monday: “The humanitarian situation is dire, with thousands of women and children in need of broad humanitarian support to survive”; noted the number of people displaced by the armed clashes in Alamata Town and Raya Alamata, Zata and Ofla since the weekend has passed 50,000.

a4666.speaker: Ethiopian federal government and Tigrayan authorities (non-response)
a4666.name: Ethiopian federal government and Tigrayan authorities (non-response)
a4666.speech: Neither the federal government nor Tigrayan authorities responded to AFP requests for information, and the identity of the fighters involved remains unclear.

a4666.speaker: Embassies of the United States, Japan, Britain and France
a4666.name: Embassies of the United States
a4666.title: Japan, Britain and France
a4666.speech: On Saturday called for dialogue and urged the “de-escalation and protection of civilians.”

a4666.speaker: Amhara regional administration (statement)
a4666.name: Amhara regional administration (statement)
a4666.speech: Last week accused the Tigray People's Liberation Front party of “invading” Raya Alamata and other areas “which have identity questions”; “The Amhara region administration asks TPLF and its supporters to... fully adhere to the Pretoria agreement and hence to swiftly vacate from the areas it currently controls” ; “If this doesn't happen the Amhara region administration will be forced... to protect our people from attack and save the country from destruction.”

a4666.speaker: Getachew Reda, senior TPLF member and head of the Tigray regional administration
a4666.name: Getachew Reda
a4666.title: senior TPLF member and head of the Tigray regional administration
a4666.speech: Said on X last week that the recent developments were “the work of diehard enemies of the Pretoria agreement trying to take advantage of real or perceived differences to derail” the peace deal.

a4852.speaker: Fasika Sidelel, former head of the economy at the time
a4852.name: Fasika Sidelel
a4852.title: former head of the economy at the time
a4852.speech: Recalled a USAID report from the time that praised the Relief & Rehabilitation Commission's efforts as an "excellent effort," a tribute to Hailemariam's front-line oversight.

a4852.speaker: Shibeshi Lemma, public relations head of the Relief & Rehabilitation Commission at the time
a4852.name: Shibeshi Lemma
a4852.title: public relations head of the Relief & Rehabilitation Commission at the time
a4852.speech: Spoke of Hailemariam with reverence, recalling his dedication to duty even at great personal sacrifice, and that discipline, time management, and a tireless journey to the countryside on treacherous, underdeveloped roads were not things that anyone could do ; "It required selflessness," said Shibeshi.
