"Hailemariam did it."

a4852.speaker: Yohannes Hailemariam, son of Hailemariam Seifu
a4852.name: Yohannes Hailemariam
a4852.title: son of Hailemariam Seifu
a4852.speech: Says they understood that their father was given to the country, not just the family ; recalled the moments of connection and lessons learned during road trips across Ethiopia, and the conversations and driving lessons they would engage in along with his younger brother: "The trips were one of our bonding moments."

a4852.speaker: Yohannes Hailemariam, son of Hailemariam Seifu
a4852.name: Yohannes Hailemariam
a4852.title: son of Hailemariam Seifu
a4852.speech: Said of his father's writing: "It's his way of getting relief from a stressful environment."

a4852.speaker: Hailemariam Seifu, founding member and longtime emergency response desk head of the Relief & Rehabilitation Commission
a4852.name: Hailemariam Seifu
a4852.title: founding member and longtime emergency response desk head of the Relief & Rehabilitation Commission
a4852.speech: "I've never done anything that will make you ashamed," he would tell his family in the months before his passing on January 28, 2024. "You'll walk tall and proud."

a4930.speaker: US Government (at the 2002 Monterrey Summit)
a4930.name: US Government (at the 2002 Monterrey Summit)
a4930.speech: called for a "new contract for international development" establishing a link between greater contributions from developed nations and greater responsibility on the part of developing countries ; committed to substantially increasing development aid.

a4930.speaker: Millennium Challenge Account (MCA selection criteria)
a4930.name: Millennium Challenge Account (MCA selection criteria)
a4930.speech: The countries selected are those that "demonstrate good governance, promote a free economy and take care of their populations" ("ruling justly, fostering economic freedom, and investing in their citizens").

a4963.speaker: Monday Semaya, South Sudan's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a4963.name: Monday Semaya
a4963.title: South Sudan's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a4963.speech: Says his recent visit to the United States was intended to amend relations and promote South Sudan as an investment destination for American investors in oil, gas and infrastructure; said he held high-level meetings at the U.S. State Department with a senior presidential advisor and deputy assistant secretary of state for African affairs in an effort to have the American government lift the blanket visa ban for all South Sudanese passport holders: "I was visiting the United States this time mainly to reset the bilateral relations between our two countries … to find possibilities of lifting the visa restrictions and also to coordinate our efforts in addressing the challenges facing the Republic of South Sudan within the United Nations family."

a4963.speaker: Monday Semaya, South Sudan's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a4963.name: Monday Semaya
a4963.title: South Sudan's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a4963.speech: Said he held meetings with American business leaders, during which he highlighted oil, gas, minerals, and infrastructure development as investment opportunities: "And most importantly, I was visiting the United States this time to also offer an opportunity to the United States government and the United States investors to come and invest in the Republic of South Sudan with main focus in areas of minerals, oil and gas, tourism, agriculture, and infrastructure development, among others" ; according to Semaya, his proposals were received positively by U.S. officials.

a4963.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a4963.name: Marco Rubio
a4963.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a4963.speech: Two weeks ago reaffirmed the enduring friendship between the American and South Sudanese people—a bond he said began long before South Sudan's independence in 2011; in a message shared via the official Facebook page of the U.S. Embassy in Juba on July 9th, Rubio extended his best wishes to the people of South Sudan on behalf of the U.S. Government.

a5000.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a5000.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a5000.title: President of Somalia
a5000.speech: Announced that Somalia's executive and legislative branches have approved a crucial 10-year defense and economic cooperation agreement with Turkey; speaking to the media, he noted Turkey is already helping Somalia with humanitarian assistance, budgetary support and the training of security forces.

a5000.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a5000.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a5000.title: President of Somalia
a5000.speech: Said the agreement with Turkey is not aimed against Ethiopia: "We asked for the support not to fight Ethiopia or invade another country. It's to support us in defending our country. That is the origin of the agreement we have entered with Turkey." ; Said Somalia has been looking for a country to enter with a bilateral agreement on building a navy and that Turkey was the first country ready to help; asked whether the deal between Somaliland and Ethiopia prompted the agreement, he said the government has been working on the agreement for some time: "It's just a coincidence."

a5000.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Somali Prime Minister
a5000.name: Hamza Abdi Barre
a5000.title: Somali Prime Minister
a5000.speech: Addressing members of the cabinet, said that under the agreement Turkey will build, train and equip the Somali navy, and that the agreement will help to remove "any fears of terrorism, piracy, illegal fishing, toxic dumping and any external violations or threats" to Somalia's sea coast; he described Turkey as a "true and reliable brother."

a5000.speaker: Somaliland
a5000.name: Somaliland
a5000.speech: Said that in exchange for leasing landlocked Ethiopia about 20 kilometers of coastline along the Gulf of Aden, Ethiopia would recognize Somaliland as an independent country.

a5000.speaker: Somalia's federal government
a5000.name: Somalia's federal government
a5000.speech: Considers Somaliland part of its own territory, sees the Ethiopia-Somaliland deal as a violation of sovereignty and is demanding its cancellation.

a5000.speaker: Somali official (anonymous, spoke to VOA Somali on condition of anonymity)
a5000.name: Somali official (anonymous
a5000.title: spoke to VOA Somali on condition of anonymity)
a5000.speech: Said the agreement includes deployment of Turkish warships in Somalia's waters, and that it also includes "tapping marine resources for Somalia."

a5000.speaker: Yasar Guler, Turkey Minister of National Defense
a5000.name: Yasar Guler
a5000.title: Turkey Minister of National Defense
a5000.speech: Said at the time of the February 8 signing that he believes the deal will lead to the further development of "our bilateral military relations."

a5000.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopian Prime Minister (message posted on X)
a5000.name: Abiy Ahmed
a5000.title: Ethiopian Prime Minister (message posted on X)
a5000.speech: Recently said his country does not intend to cause harm to Somalia: "Ethiopia, being a friend, does not wish any harm to come upon Somalia." ; "Ethiopia does not acknowledge war against any country in principle. However, some forces are trying to incite conflict between the two nations, which should not happen. Our request is for sea access based on mutual benefit."

a5000.speaker: Turkey (official position)
a5000.name: Turkey (official position)
a5000.speech: Said its engagement with Somali forces is to contribute to peace and stability in Somalia and improve the organization and infrastructure of the Somali National Army as it battles al-Shabab militants.

a5000.speaker: Hussein Sheikh-Ali, national security adviser to Somalia's president
a5000.name: Hussein Sheikh-Ali
a5000.title: national security adviser to Somalia's president
a5000.speech: Told VOA last week that the U.S. will train 3,000 soldiers, most of whom have already completed the training, and that the aim is to start building the bases soon and finish within the calendar year: "It would look like a military camp with a full capacity to host special forces." ; He also said Somali security forces are aiming to assume responsibilities from the African Union Transition Mission (ATMIS), which is expected to withdraw from Somalia by the end of 2024.

a5042.speaker: Hanna Arayaselassie, Commissioner of the Ethiopian Investment Commission
a5042.name: Hanna Arayaselassie
a5042.title: Commissioner of the Ethiopian Investment Commission
a5042.speech: Announced over 3.8 billion dollars in foreign direct investment during the ended fiscal year, reflecting an 11.5pc growth compared to the previous year, and, though it fell short of the annual target by 20pc, expressed optimism about the upward trend, solidifying Ethiopia's position as a leading FDI destination in Africa.

a5042.speaker: Hanna Arayaselassie, Commissioner of the Ethiopian Investment Commission
a5042.name: Hanna Arayaselassie
a5042.title: Commissioner of the Ethiopian Investment Commission
a5042.speech: Acknowledged that export revenues from industrial parks fell below expectations due to Ethiopia's exclusion from the African Growth & Opportunity Act (AGOA).

a5042.speaker: Hanna Arayaselassie, Commissioner of the Ethiopian Investment Commission
a5042.name: Hanna Arayaselassie
a5042.title: Commissioner of the Ethiopian Investment Commission
a5042.speech: Plans to diversify the manufacturing-dominated sector in the coming fiscal year and is determined to further enhance investment promotion and raise FDI to 4.5 billion dollars in the fiscal year, by implementing new regulations, streamlining logistics and incentives, and developing a digitisation plan.

a5293.speaker: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5293.name: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5293.speech: condemned and denounced the statements of US President Donald Trump regarding his call for the displacement of the Palestinian people outside the Gaza Strip, his support for alleged Israeli sovereignty over Palestinian land, and the suspension of funding for UNRWA, considering that this contributes to entrenching the occupation, colonial settlement and the forcible seizure of Palestinian land, which constitutes a flagrant violation of the principles of international law and the relevant United Nations resolutions, including Security Council Resolution 2334, and is likely to undermine the chances of peace and destabilise the region.

a5293.speaker: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5293.name: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5293.speech: expressed its strict rejection of all plans aimed at changing the geographical, demographic or legal reality of the occupied Palestinian territory. It stressed that the Gaza Strip is an integral part of the occupied State of Palestine, and called for concerted efforts to establish a comprehensive and sustainable ceasefire, the complete withdrawal of the Israeli occupation, the strengthening of the steadfastness of the Palestinians on their land and their safe return to their homes, the provision of urgently needed aid, economic recovery and the reconstruction of the Gaza Strip, as well as ensuring accountability for all crimes committed by the Israeli occupation against the Palestinian people.

a5293.speaker: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5293.name: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5293.speech: renewed its unwavering support for UNRWA and its central and irreplaceable role and expressed its strict rejection of all attempts to undermine its existence or its legal mandate. It regards the relief agency as a top priority in humanitarian aid, as testimony to the international commitment to the rights of Palestinian refugees and as an element of stability in the region.

a5293.speaker: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5293.name: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5293.speech: reaffirmed its absolute solidarity with the Palestinian people and its unwavering support for their just struggle within the framework of the Palestine Liberation Organization, the sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people, for the restoration of their inalienable rights, including their right to self-determination and the embodiment of the sovereignty of the independent State of Palestine within the borders of June 1967, including the Gaza Strip, the West Bank and East Jerusalem as its capital. It renewed its commitment to supporting international efforts aimed at a just, lasting and comprehensive peace in the region, leading to an end to the Israeli occupation and the implementation of a two-state solution on the basis of the principles of international law, the Charter of the United Nations and its relevant resolutions, as well as the Arab Peace Initiative.

a5609.speaker: World Igbo Congress (WIC) and other international groups, backed by religious leaders, academic experts and human rights lawyers (joint statement)
a5609.name: World Igbo Congress (WIC) and other international groups
a5609.title: backed by religious leaders, academic experts and human rights lawyers (joint statement)
a5609.speech: joined the International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety) in condemning in strongest terms the extrajudicial killings, forced disappearance and destructions in Nigeria's South-East region by state actors and non-state actors; while expressing support for Intersociety's reports on the “Warzone Situation” in Eastern Nigeria, called on the United Nations and the International Criminal Court (ICC) to investigate the issues raised in the reports ; “We hereby call on the UN Special Rapporteur on Extrajudicial, Summary or Arbitrary Executions; the UN Special Rapporteur on Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment; the UN Special Rapporteur on Human Rights and Religious Freedom; the UN Special Rapporteur on Human Rights Defenders; the UN Special Rapporteur on Human Rights of the Internally Displaced People; the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Arrest and Detention; the UN Special Rapporteur on the Right to Adequate Housing (anti-Domicide)... and the Chief Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) to urgently intervene, investigate and identify and hold armed state actor and armed non-state actor perpetrators involved accountable and sanction public office holders found in the Reports to have aided, abetted and sponsored such grievous crimes or conduct-atrocities and have them sanctioned appropriately.”

a5609.speaker: World Igbo Congress (WIC) and other international groups (joint statement)
a5609.name: World Igbo Congress (WIC) and other international groups (joint statement)
a5609.speech: urged the incoming US President Donald Trump's administration to adopt the Intersociety's reports as working documents on human rights and international development partnership policies on Nigeria and its government: “We also urge the incoming Trump Administration in the United States to adopt the Reports as working documents in the assessment of Nigeria’s human rights records and the USA’s future international development partnership with the Government of Nigeria. The incoming Donald Administration is particularly called upon to ensure that the Government of Nigeria and the country’s security forces’ high commands are compelled to respect the International Freedom of Worship or Belief and end such discrimination or risk being enlisted in the USA’s ‘Country Of Particular Concern (CPC)’ under her International Religious Freedom Act (IRFA) of 1998.”

a5609.speaker: World Igbo Congress (WIC) and other international groups (joint statement)
a5609.name: World Igbo Congress (WIC) and other international groups (joint statement)
a5609.speech: “In line with the Intersociety’s seventy-six strong recommendations contained in the Special Reports, we are calling on Nigeria’s International Development Partners including all Member-States of the EU, the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, etc., to: critically study the Reports and have them reflected in future development and defense, security and safety assistance and supports... and ensure that such development and military supports or assistance are not channeled into ‘instruments of violence or state terror and persecution’ against defenseless members of the Eastern civilian population and their properties ; The above democracies called upon are urged to ensure that such development assistance and human rights and humanitarian supports amounting to billions of dollars yearly are not channeled into extrajudicial killings, abductions, torture and other cruel treatments, enforced disappearances, civilian house burnings, false labeling, class criminalisation, ethnoreligious profiling and persecution, prosecutorial vindictiveness and hearsay conclusions, etc.”

a5609.speaker: World Igbo Congress (WIC) and other international groups (joint statement)
a5609.name: World Igbo Congress (WIC) and other international groups (joint statement)
a5609.speech: “The Government of Nigeria shall further be compelled to frontally address pandemic and endemic corruption in the country’s security (military, police and secret police) sector and digitalise law enforcement operations including preventive, detective, investigative policing and crime detection; all of which have become a modern trend in the mother world. More so, when ‘Digital Policing/Security’ has become the speediest way by which struggling countries have leveled up with advanced countries owing to the fact it is quantitative, qualitative, cheaper, available, avoidable, less corrupt, human rights and rule of law friendly and importable or exportable.”

a5609.speaker: Intersociety Special Reports, “Ocean Of Innocent Blood Flowing In Eastern Nigeria” (282 pages) and “Human Rights Made In Nigeria” (154 pages)
a5609.name: Intersociety Special Reports
a5609.title: “Ocean Of Innocent Blood Flowing In Eastern Nigeria” (282 pages) and “Human Rights Made In Nigeria” (154 pages)
a5609.speech: stated that during the period under review, “The Nigerian Security Forces (NSFs) unlawfully killed 32,300 defenseless citizens including the abducted and disappeared; tortured and bodily lacerated tens of thousands; burned down or razed 6000 civilian homes and allied properties valued at over N450 billion; raided 300 defenseless Igbo communities; sacked their 180,000 inhabitants; and frightened and forced over 1 million others to flee their homes” ; “During which, too, Government-linked and non-Government linked armed non state actors in their several thousands killed over 14,500 defenseless citizens, abducted over 65,000 others and forced estimated 55,000 of them to pay ransoms estimated at over N500 billion... and razed or burned down civilian properties valued at over N60 billion and aided by biased and compromised Nigerian Security Forces to influx and proliferate estimated 2.7m illicit Small Arms and Light Weapons across Eastern Nigeria” ; further catalogued and exposed massive arbitrary arrests, perpetual detentions, kangaroo arraignments, late night abduction and face-bagging of unarmed Igbo civilians to secret military detention facilities in northern Nigeria, torture and bodily lacerations, “open killings, secret, extralegal and extra jus executions, innumerable cases of enforced disappearances... indiscriminate false labeling, mass criminalization, class stigmatization and ethno-religious profiling”, all of which had arisen from military siege and terror in Eastern Nigeria since August 2015 using “IPOB/ESN/Biafra Terrorism” as a pretext or cover ; found that “Out of every fifteen unarmed citizens arrested by police crack squads, seven run the high risk of not returning to their families alive” and that “95% of police or military or spy police-issued security intelligence information and law enforcement operations’ reports in the South-East and the South-South are highly questionable and most likely to have been concocted or twisted or falsified.”

a5614.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a5614.title: Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.speech: asserts that while Eswatini has made strides in business growth and attracting foreign investment, the country’s greatest potential lies in its natural resources: Eswatini’s timber forests, cropland, and pastureland dominate its natural capital portfolio, valued at US$8.383 million in 2018, up significantly from 1995, driven by both renewable resources (like forests) and non-renewable resources (like coal) ; warns that the lack of a proper management framework for these resources is preventing the country from fully leveraging them to fund initiatives such as climate change mitigation.

a5614.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a5614.title: Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.speech: notes that 65% youth unemployment is driven by a mismatch between school curricula and industry needs; while gross enrolment rates are high (126% for primary and 100% for junior secondary), the average years of schooling is just six and dropout rates remain high.

a5614.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a5614.title: Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.speech: highlights high maternal mortality rates and an under-resourced public healthcare system, which present significant social and economic challenges.

a5614.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a5614.title: Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.speech: identifies finance as one of the country’s biggest constraints: four banks dominate the market, limiting competition and financial inclusion; the stock exchange is underdeveloped with low liquidity; SMEs face tough lending conditions due to strict collateral requirements; and 37% of the population remains unbanked, restricting savings and investment.

a5614.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a5614.title: Country Focused Report 2025
a5614.speech: recommends that to achieve sustainable growth Eswatini strengthen regulatory frameworks, boost competition in the financial sector, promote financial inclusion, simplify tax laws to attract investment, and partner with offshore markets for external funding, with agriculture, tourism, and renewable energy as key sectors for priority investment; also calls for vocational training to close the education–industry skills gap and a framework for managing and leveraging natural resources to fund climate change initiatives and ensure long-term sustainability.

a5818.speaker: Louis Kpoto, Liberian Health Minister
a5818.name: Louis Kpoto
a5818.title: Liberian Health Minister
a5818.speech: Described the project as transformative, stressing that decentralization of the health system needs to be enhanced and improved upon the financial management to enable full implementation of the project ; "The project will further improve the quality of data analysis and reporting in the Sector, monitoring and evaluating every step, thus making decentralization key to provide the expected results. It will also improve the quality of data analysis and reporting in the sector and drive informed decisions."

a5818.speaker: Louis Kpoto, Liberian Health Minister
a5818.name: Louis Kpoto
a5818.title: Liberian Health Minister
a5818.speech: Emphasized the need to promote transparency and accountability to increase monitoring of availability and quality of health services and commodities.

a5818.speaker: Mark Toner, US Ambassador to Liberia
a5818.name: Mark Toner
a5818.title: US Ambassador to Liberia
a5818.speech: Lauded the Health Ministry for progress made in the areas of malaria treatment and infant mortality in eight of Liberia’s fifteen counties ; "The project will build on the successes made in the Sector to improve health outcomes and service delivery in the country’s Health System." ; he then committed USAID to decentralizing house service governance by empowering local authorities to ensure that critical decisions on health are made in each county. "With collaboration, Liberia’s Health Sector will be built on sustained health care system."

a5888.speaker: Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, former Somali President
a5888.name: Sharif Sheikh Ahmed
a5888.title: former Somali President
a5888.speech: Thanked the United States for its continued support in security, counter-terrorism, and humanitarian assistance efforts in Somalia.

a5888.speaker: The United States
a5888.name: The United States
a5888.speech: Has reiterated its commitment to backing Somalia's efforts to build effective governance institutions despite persistent political and security challenges.

a5898.speaker: General Randall Reed, Commander of United States Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM)
a5898.name: General Randall Reed
a5898.title: Commander of United States Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM)
a5898.speech: Spoke about his trip to the Indo-Pacific region, notably to the Philippines and Japan, where he met senior officials and worked to strengthen logistical and security partnerships in the region ; states that United States Transportation Command gives the United States incredible strategic and responsive mobility worldwide: “The members of USTRANSCOM, together with industry, allies and partners, make us a ready, united and decisive force, capable of responding rapidly to crises and supporting humanitarian and military operations around the world.”

a5898.speaker: General Randall Reed, Commander of USTRANSCOM
a5898.name: General Randall Reed
a5898.title: Commander of USTRANSCOM
a5898.speech: Returned to the importance of allies and partners for USTRANSCOM in all its activities, saying that we cannot achieve this without very solid partnerships, and that this is precisely what motivates his travels this week ; said he explored ways to strengthen collaboration, deter any aggression and improve preparedness for any potential crisis in the region, and looks forward to having the same discussions during his visit to the Republic of Korea ; said what is essential in his eyes is the complexity of this region, which requires multidimensional solutions involving many partners: “It is essential to maintain and develop our relationships in the region, because we cooperate and collaborate to guarantee a rapid United States response to any future humanitarian assistance and disaster relief operation, while fighting threats to international peace and security, whether they come from state actors, violent extremist groups or others.”

a5898.speaker: General Randall Reed, Commander of USTRANSCOM
a5898.name: General Randall Reed
a5898.title: Commander of USTRANSCOM
a5898.speech: Said that with his counterparts they discussed ways of continuing cooperation through standing defence agreements and of further strengthening the logistics system; that this summer they plan to conduct a series of exercises to test the current logistical architecture and infrastructure, which provide sustainable freedom of manoeuvre in the region and to the joint force; that the objective is to have the capacity to mobilise rapidly and then deploy forces from the United States to sites distributed throughout the region; that these exercises will be essential to test tactics, techniques and procedures with allies and partners and to improve connectivity between different sites in the region; and that TRANSCOM is a learning organisation that helps deepen relationships and collaborate even more closely to strengthen regional security. “Thus, thanks to continued support, we will retain the capacity to react at any time, whatever the need”, he concluded.

a5907.speaker: Abu Anwar Muhammad Al-Ghazali, University of The Gambia School of Medicine and Allied Health Sciences (letter to the editor)
a5907.name: Abu Anwar Muhammad Al-Ghazali
a5907.title: University of The Gambia School of Medicine and Allied Health Sciences (letter to the editor)
a5907.speech: Argued that African education remains marred by a colonial legacy that “perpetuates their control, alienating and limiting our potential through an education model that was never designed for African progress”, produced “obedient workers rather than innovators”, and teaches irrelevant content while students are “not taught how to mine or process the copper they walk over on their way to school”.

a5907.speaker: Abu Anwar Muhammad Al-Ghazali, University of The Gambia School of Medicine and Allied Health Sciences (letter to the editor)
a5907.name: Abu Anwar Muhammad Al-Ghazali
a5907.title: University of The Gambia School of Medicine and Allied Health Sciences (letter to the editor)
a5907.speech: Wrote that when the system “inevitably fails to prepare us for real-world challenges, we find ourselves dependent on foreign aid and loans, which only serve to deepen our economic bondage”, and that the colonial model “was explicitly designed to perpetuate African dependence on Western economies” and inculcates “a mentality of inferiority”.

a5907.speaker: Abu Anwar Muhammad Al-Ghazali, University of The Gambia School of Medicine and Allied Health Sciences (letter to the editor)
a5907.name: Abu Anwar Muhammad Al-Ghazali
a5907.title: University of The Gambia School of Medicine and Allied Health Sciences (letter to the editor)
a5907.speech: Urged that “to achieve true liberation, we must reimagine and revolutionize of education systems from ground up”, prioritising knowledge that harnesses African resources and reclaiming African histories, philosophies and sciences – “by Africans, for Africans—fostering a mindset of independence, resilience, and self-determination rather than dependency.”

a5907.speaker: Madi Jobarteh, Kembujeh (letter to the editor, re: Government names companies licensed to recruit workers to Spain)
a5907.name: Madi Jobarteh
a5907.title: Kembujeh (letter to the editor, re: Government names companies licensed to recruit workers to Spain)
a5907.speech: Asked “Why should would we send our men and women to do farming in Spain when we have enough arable land and water here to farm in the country?”, argued the government should invest adequately in agriculture and entice people into farming, questioned what support government gives farmers in mechanised farming, and called the arrangement “a so-called agreement” than which “there cannot be a more irresponsible decision”.

a5907.speaker: Yero S Bah, Nema Kunku (letter to the editor, re: Government names companies licensed to recruit workers to Spain)
a5907.name: Yero S Bah
a5907.title: Nema Kunku (letter to the editor, re: Government names companies licensed to recruit workers to Spain)
a5907.speech: Wrote that “this whole scheme shows our lack of long-term vision for a country”, reporting from Europe that there are “hundreds of thousands, if not millions, of migrants without jobs in Spain, Portugal, Italy and France” and that “the Europe that is sold in The Gambia or Africa is not the one most find here.”

a5913.speaker: East African Community (EAC) (communique)
a5913.name: East African Community (EAC) (communique)
a5913.speech: Said the facilitator, former president of Kenya Uhuru Kenyatta, met with armed groups, civil society, and victims of sexual violence; that it was agreed community leaders, DRC government officials and EAC officials must form a committee to “facilitate the release of prisoners with no criminal records of atrocities and, or criminal convictions”; that DRC President Felix Tshisekedi was asked to engage communities in eco-friendly projects and conservation and, in Maniema province, should meet local leadership to “discuss how the community can be involved in and benefit from the mining industry in the region”; that rebel leaders should be considered as stakeholders to avoid conflict; that the priority was the release of child soldiers by all armed militia groups while the cessation of hostilities continued; and that humanitarian assistance should start flowing soon into communities cut off by the conflict, with a review of the targets in January in Bunia and Goma before a medium- and long-term roadmap is put in place.

a5946.speaker: The organisers
a5946.name: The organisers
a5946.speech: According to the organisers, the partnership between the Red Cross, USAID, and IFRC represents a push to combat climate change and preserve the environment, showcasing a collective commitment to a sustainable future.

a5946.speaker: Abdoulie Fye, acting secretary general of the Gambia Red Cross Society (GRCS)
a5946.name: Abdoulie Fye
a5946.title: acting secretary general of the Gambia Red Cross Society (GRCS)
a5946.speech: Said the primary motivation for the initiative is to combat the devastating effects of climate change; said climate change has a severe impact on local communities, and addressing it should be the business of everybody: “Today, we are here to plant trees and help them grow to provide the necessary benefit to the community.”

a5946.speaker: Njogou Jeng, national society development officer for IFRC
a5946.name: Njogou Jeng
a5946.title: national society development officer for IFRC
a5946.speech: Highlighted efforts to enhance the resilience of communities, particularly in the face of climate impacts: “The trees are very important in society. As you all know, we cannot live without the presence of the trees, because they serve as windbreakers, firewood, among others.”

a5946.speaker: Oumie Touray, a community representative in Kartong
a5946.name: Oumie Touray
a5946.title: a community representative in Kartong
a5946.speech: Said without trees the rain patterns will be very low and human beings would not receive the needed carbohydrates coming from trees.

a5983.speaker: Lisa Johnson, United States Ambassador to Namibia
a5983.name: Lisa Johnson
a5983.title: United States Ambassador to Namibia
a5983.speech: “This assistance came from a programme called ‘Defense’s humanitarian assistance’ of the United States. Such assistance is given in order to help wherever there is a need to fight the Covid-19 disease across the whole country.”

a5983.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a5983.name: Ben Nangombe
a5983.title: Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a5983.speech: Confirmed that all the donations were given to the hospitals that are truly in need.

a5983.speaker: Eric Dziuban, head of the U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention in Namibia
a5983.name: Eric Dziuban
a5983.title: head of the U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention in Namibia
a5983.speech: Said their agency is working together with the Namibian government to fight the disease ; “We are prepared to fight the Covid-19 disease, and the advice we give to the public is only that citizens should wash their hands all the time and keep away from places where many people gather.”

a5989.speaker: Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, President of Egypt
a5989.name: Abdel Fattah al-Sisi
a5989.title: President of Egypt
a5989.speech: “In recent days, Egypt has worked to launch an initiative aimed at promoting a 48-hour ceasefire, under which four hostages would be exchanged for a group of prisoners in Israeli jails,” said the President of Egypt during a press conference in Cairo with his Algerian counterpart, Abdelmadjid Tebboune ; Added that negotiations will be held over 10 days to discuss a series of measures to be applied in the Gaza Strip “in order to reach a comprehensive ceasefire” ; “As regards Gaza, there is an Arab consensus on the importance of a ceasefire and of the entry of humanitarian aid, in addition to the release of the hostages and of Palestinian prisoners,” reiterating that the ongoing truce negotiations are also addressing “the dangers” of an escalation of violence in the Middle East ; Recalled that the Palestinians of the devastated enclave “are under a heavy siege that extends as far as starvation”: “That is why the arrival of humanitarian aid is important,” insisting that his country rejects “any attempt at forced displacement” of Gaza’s inhabitants.

a5989.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a5989.name: Antony Blinken
a5989.title: US Secretary of State
a5989.speech: Called for the death of Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar to be seized upon in order to restart the negotiations and put an end to the war.

a5989.speaker: AFP count based on official Israeli figures
a5989.name: AFP count based on official Israeli figures
a5989.speech: The Hamas attack of 7 October 2023 caused the deaths of 1,206 people, most of them civilians, according to an AFP count based on official Israeli figures.

a5989.speaker: Health Ministry of the Hamas-run territory of Gaza (figures the United Nations considers reliable)
a5989.name: Health Ministry of the Hamas-run territory of Gaza (figures the United Nations considers reliable)
a5989.speech: Since then, the Israeli offensive in Gaza has killed at least 42,924 Palestinians, most of them civilians, according to the figures of the Health Ministry of the Hamas-run territory, which the United Nations considers reliable.

a5999.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5999.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a5999.title: Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5999.speech: Said in a weekly post-Cabinet briefing that distribution of inputs under the Presidential Pfumvudza/Intwasa programme for the 2024/25 summer cropping season is currently ongoing in all parts of the country and that the move dovetails with the government thrust to increase productivity ; "Meanwhile, distribution of Presidential Inputs including cotton has commenced. Progress with the Silo expansion project is on course at the following depots, Kwekwe, Mutare Grain, Mhangura, Mvurwi, Timbermills, Lupane and Rutenga. On cotton, a total of 427 550 farmers will be supported through contract farming with a target covering an area of 278 750 hectare."

a5999.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5999.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a5999.title: Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5999.speech: Said the government aims to increase production of cereals to 3 274 200 metric tons from 744 271 metric tons in the 2023/24 season ; "The overall production volumes of major crops are expected to increase by 347 percent. The plan is to produce enough to feed the nation and to replenish the Strategic Grain Reserve. The country expects to receive normal to above normal rainfall during this season."

a5999.speaker: Dr Anxious Masuka, Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development Minister
a5999.name: Dr Anxious Masuka
a5999.title: Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development Minister
a5999.speech: Said following rains received recently, planting has started across the country ; "A few areas that have not received sufficient rain to start planting, but this is just isolated patches throughout the country. So this whole sector has mobilised resources, particularly for the Presidential Input programme. 58 percent of the fertilisers are available and of that fertiliser 75 percent has been distributed. 90 percent of the maize seed has been received and of that 80 percent has already been distributed." ; "Similarly, for cotton inputs we have received over 80 percent of those inputs and distribution is ongoing. So countrywide farmers are naturally excited."

a5999.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5999.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a5999.title: Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5999.speech: Said national grain stocks at the Grain Marketing Board (GMB) stand at 253 665 metric tons ; "Cabinet highlights that a total of 1 036 721 metric tonnes, comprising 852 260 metric tonnes of maize, 184 121 metric tonnes of wheat and 340 metric tonnes of wheat flour were imported by the private sector as at 20 November, 2024. To date, 885 import permits have been issued to 423 companies to import 4 430 280 metric tonnes of maize against the deficit of 1 million metric tonnes. Government continues to monitor volumes of imports, stocks at millers, import prices, and import sources ahead of the festive season in order to eliminate arbitrage opportunities."

a6280.speaker: Health experts (panellists, DS-I Africa consortium meeting, Accra)
a6280.name: Health experts (panellists
a6280.title: DS-I Africa consortium meeting, Accra)
a6280.speech: Made a case for governments on the continent to invest in health data science to improve health outcomes ; said that with the growing burden of chronic diseases on the continent, tailoring treatments based on individual patient characteristics and genetic profiles had become necessary ; added that increasing investment in data infrastructure, and addressing skills gaps could help in timely disease prediction and prevention.

a6280.speaker: Prof. Kofi A. Amengah, associate professor of Environmental and Nutritional Epidemiology, University of Cape Coast (UCC)
a6280.name: Prof. Kofi A. Amengah
a6280.title: associate professor of Environmental and Nutritional Epidemiology, University of Cape Coast (UCC)
a6280.speech: Said significant barriers existed on the continent in areas such as data quality, access and funding. “These are the elephants in the room that must be addressed for data science to make a meaningful impact on health outcomes,” he said.

a6280.speaker: Prof. Kofi A. Amengah, associate professor of Environmental and Nutritional Epidemiology, University of Cape Coast (UCC)
a6280.name: Prof. Kofi A. Amengah
a6280.title: associate professor of Environmental and Nutritional Epidemiology, University of Cape Coast (UCC)
a6280.speech: Said that the DS-I project planned to publish 18 manuscripts in prestigious journals, and also produce policy briefs for health ministries across Africa, the World Health Organisation and other stakeholders.

a6280.speaker: Prof. Kofi A. Amengah, associate professor of Environmental and Nutritional Epidemiology, University of Cape Coast (UCC)
a6280.name: Prof. Kofi A. Amengah
a6280.title: associate professor of Environmental and Nutritional Epidemiology, University of Cape Coast (UCC)
a6280.speech: Urged the public to recognise the relevance of data science in their daily lives. “Understanding how data science can improve health is crucial. It can lead to reduced healthcare costs, which ultimately affects everyone's pocket.”

a6280.speaker: Prof. Mayowa Owolabi, Professor of Neurology, College of Medicine, University of Ibadan, Nigeria
a6280.name: Prof. Mayowa Owolabi
a6280.title: Professor of Neurology, College of Medicine, University of Ibadan, Nigeria
a6280.speech: Stressed the need to integrate data science into health policy, particularly in monitoring non-communicable diseases such as stroke, diabetes and obesity.

a6280.speaker: Prof. Mayowa Owolabi, Professor of Neurology, College of Medicine, University of Ibadan, Nigeria
a6280.name: Prof. Mayowa Owolabi
a6280.title: Professor of Neurology, College of Medicine, University of Ibadan, Nigeria
a6280.speech: Described the recent withdrawal of USAID support to Africa as a major challenge for health initiatives across the continent.

a6280.speaker: Prof. Mayowa Owolabi, Professor of Neurology, College of Medicine, University of Ibadan, Nigeria
a6280.name: Prof. Mayowa Owolabi
a6280.title: Professor of Neurology, College of Medicine, University of Ibadan, Nigeria
a6280.speech: Urged governments to recognise the economic benefits of investing in data science tools, and that preventing health issues could ultimately save money in acute care costs, adding that “health is wealth”.

a6298.speaker: Sudanese activists
a6298.name: Sudanese activists
a6298.speech: Reported on Tuesday the death of more than 50 people since violent fighting broke out on Sunday between the army and the paramilitaries in central Sudan.

a6298.speaker: Local resistance committee of Wad Madani (pro-democracy group, statement sent to AFP)
a6298.name: Local resistance committee of Wad Madani (pro-democracy group
a6298.title: statement sent to AFP)
a6298.speech: Said on Tuesday that an army airstrike on a mosque in Wad Madani killed at least 31 people on Sunday ; said the attack took place "after the evening prayers" in this town in Al-Jazira State, south of Khartoum, accusing the army of having used barrels filled with explosives ; said more than half of the victims had not been identified, with rescue workers struggling to identify "dozens of charred and mutilated bodily remains."

a6298.speaker: Resistance committee of the town of Rufaa
a6298.name: Resistance committee of the town of Rufaa
a6298.speech: Said for its part that at least 20 people had been killed in paramilitary attacks in several villages of the area since Sunday.

a6298.speaker: Sudanese army
a6298.name: Sudanese army
a6298.speech: Announced on Sunday that the RSF commander in Al-Jazira, Abou Aqla Kaykal, had abandoned the paramilitaries, with "a large number of his forces" joining the opposing camp, in what it described as the first high-level defection within the RSF.

a6298.speaker: Spokesman for General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan
a6298.name: Spokesman for General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan
a6298.speech: Said that Mr Kaykal and the others who had followed him would benefit from an "amnesty."

a6298.speaker: Paramilitary source (anonymous), to AFP
a6298.name: Paramilitary source (anonymous)
a6298.title: to AFP
a6298.speech: Said that on Tuesday the RSF had "repelled an attempt by the army" to retake the town of Tamboul, 75 kilometres north of Wad Madani.

a6298.speaker: Witness (anonymous), to AFP
a6298.name: Witness (anonymous)
a6298.title: to AFP
a6298.speech: Said the paramilitaries were "unleashed"; they "fired randomly into the air" and forced civilians to carry looted goods.

a6298.speaker: Local resistance committee of Rufaa
a6298.name: Local resistance committee of Rufaa
a6298.speech: Accused the RSF of carrying out "operations (...) against defenceless civilians" in revenge for Mr Kaykal's defection.

a6298.speaker: The Central Human Rights Observatory (volunteer group)
a6298.name: The Central Human Rights Observatory (volunteer group)
a6298.speech: Said that at least seven towns and villages in the area had been hit by "revenge attacks (...) in violation of all agreements aimed at protecting civilians and of international humanitarian law."

a6298.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a6298.name: United Nations (UN)
a6298.speech: According to the UN, the conflict has left tens of thousands dead and displaced more than 10 million people.

a6746.speaker: World Bank
a6746.name: World Bank
a6746.speech: Has flagged Malawi as one of the countries most negatively affected by the uncontrolled proliferation of aid agencies and fragmented donor-funded projects ; in an article titled 'Defragmenting the global aid architecture' published on its website, warned that the complexity of global aid flows is undermining national planning and weakening public institutions ; said that from 2019 to 2023 Malawi managed an average of 184 donor agencies, yet most of the financial support from these actors by-passed government systems, and that rather than flowing through the national budget, a growing share of development assistance has been channelled through non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and vertical funding platforms with narrow thematic focuses ; cites Dowa District, which hosts 48 domestic and international NGOs collectively reaching about 70 000 beneficiaries, but often without a unified framework or shared baseline, as exemplifying the strain this fragmentation places on local authorities.

a6746.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, economist
a6746.name: Velli Nyirongo
a6746.title: economist
a6746.speech: Said the growing reliance on off-budget donor financing is hampering the government's ability to coordinate and prioritise development interventions at national and district levels: "When aid flows bypass the government's budgeting process, it becomes difficult for authorities to gain a clear and comprehensive picture of available resources. This undermines coordinated planning, weakens alignment with national priorities, and reduces the accountability of aid flows to domestic institutions and citizens."

a6746.speaker: Stallichi Mwambiwa, Dowa district commissioner
a6746.name: Stallichi Mwambiwa
a6746.title: Dowa district commissioner
a6746.speech: In an interview, expressed concern about duplicated efforts and misaligned donor interventions, calling for greater integration of development assistance with district implementation plans.

a6746.speaker: Gilbert Kachamba, economist
a6746.name: Gilbert Kachamba
a6746.title: economist
a6746.speech: Called for reforms that enhance data transparency, strengthen budget execution systems and invest in human resources within district councils: "Clearer frameworks for donor coordination, combined with stronger leadership and ownership by local authorities, would help ensure that aid contributes more effectively to development goals."

a6998.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and Malawi Conference of Catholic Bishops (MCCB)
a6998.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and Malawi Conference of Catholic Bishops (MCCB)
a6998.speech: Have demanded action on the perpetrators of acts of violence against demonstrators in Lilongwe on Thursday.

a6998.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) (statement on Friday)
a6998.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) (statement on Friday)
a6998.speech: Said the failure by Malawi Police Service and Malawi Defence Force (MDF) officers to protect protesters is a betrayal of public trust and a stain on their constitutional mandate ; further demanded the police to act immediately and decisively to arrest all those involved in the violence, regardless of their political affiliations ; “The continued failure to bring these assailants to justice points directly to political protection from the highest levels of power in the governing party.”

a6998.speaker: Malawi Conference of Catholic Bishops (MCCB) (statement on Saturday)
a6998.name: Malawi Conference of Catholic Bishops (MCCB) (statement on Saturday)
a6998.speech: Said all citizens should be mindful of the fragile nature of peace and should honour democratic processes ahead of the September 16 2025 General Election ; “We call upon security agencies not to abrogate their duty by paying a blind eye to criminal activities. Such behaviour not only fuels impunity but also erodes public trust in them.”

a6998.speaker: Archbishop Thomas Luke Msusa, Catholic Church Archdiocese of Blantyre
a6998.name: Archbishop Thomas Luke Msusa
a6998.title: Catholic Church Archdiocese of Blantyre
a6998.speech: Delivering a homily at St Peter and St Paul Parish in Chilobwe Township in Blantyre, encouraged Christians to pray for peaceful elections and have hope that God will hear the prayers.

a6998.speaker: The European Union, US, UK and seven other foreign missions
a6998.name: The European Union
a6998.title: US, UK and seven other foreign missions
a6998.speech: Expressed alarm over the trend of violence during demonstrations.

a6998.speaker: Malawi Law Society
a6998.name: Malawi Law Society
a6998.speech: Demanded decisive action, including the dismissal of Minister of Homeland Security Ezekiel Ching'oma and Police Inspector General Merlyne Yolamu.

a6998.speaker: Citizens for Credible Elections (protesters)
a6998.name: Citizens for Credible Elections (protesters)
a6998.speech: Gathered to demand the resignation of Malawi Electoral Commission chairperson Justice Annabel Mtalimanja and chief elections officer Andrew Mpesi.

a6998.speaker: Footage and photographs from the scene
a6998.name: Footage and photographs from the scene
a6998.speech: Show that MPS and MDF officers at the scene were largely inactive, besides throwing a few rounds of tear gas.

a6998.speaker: President Lazarus Chakwera (post on his official Facebook page on Saturday)
a6998.name: President Lazarus Chakwera (post on his official Facebook page on Saturday)
a6998.speech: Said he has directed all relevant State agencies to investigate what happened.

a7043.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7043.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7043.title: President of Ghana
a7043.speech: Announced two new national initiatives aimed at helping to strengthen Ghana's health financing — the Presidential High-Level Task Force on Global Health Governance and the Sustain Initiative (Scaling Up Sovereign Transitions and Institutional Networks) — saying the task force would serve as a platform to engage both global and continental partners to reshape health governance systems, with the goal of responding to today's realities rather than relying on outdated structures, and explaining that the Sustain Initiative would align national budgets with health priorities, help mobilise domestic, diaspora, and philanthropic funding into health systems, support cross-border learning and improve accountability.

a7043.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7043.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7043.title: President of Ghana
a7043.speech: “The world has changed, but global health governance has not kept pace. We are called to redesign a system that has for too long ignored Africa's voice, needs, and innovations.” He cited global challenges such as pandemics, conflict, climate shocks, and economic instability as signs of a system under strain, saying these pressures demand a new approach that supports resilience, fairness, and human dignity.

a7043.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7043.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7043.title: President of Ghana
a7043.speech: Referenced a sharp drop in global development assistance in 2023, which he said had immediate effects across Africa, noting that in many countries, including Ghana, funding cuts disrupted maternal health services, delayed vaccines, and left hospitals with drug shortages: “In Ghana, our community-based health delivery system, known as the CHPS Compound Programme, nearly collapsed after donor withdrawals.”

a7043.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7043.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7043.title: President of Ghana
a7043.speech: Said the government had since taken steps to protect the health sector by unlocking more domestic resources: “We have uncapped our National Health Insurance Scheme financing, opening up an additional GH¢3.5 billion for broader coverage.”

a7043.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7043.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7043.title: President of Ghana
a7043.speech: Disclosed that Ghana would introduce a new primary healthcare programme in the coming months, with technical support from the World Health Organisation (WHO), and announced plans to deploy community health volunteers to promote preventive care and wellness services.

a7043.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a7043.name: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a7043.title: WHO Director-General
a7043.speech: Had committed to sending a team to support the design process of Ghana's new primary healthcare programme.

a7043.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7043.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7043.title: President of Ghana
a7043.speech: Sharing a local example, said a young mother in Dodowa had survived childbirth complications because the local CHPS facility was digitally linked to a regional hospital: “This is not a future vision. It is already happening. This is health sovereignty in action.”

a7043.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7043.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7043.title: President of Ghana
a7043.speech: Argued that governments must treat health spending as an investment, not a cost: “Health is wealth. We must change the thinking that health weakens economies.” He also called for stronger support for platforms such as PanaBIOS for health verification, Propa for supply chain monitoring, and BioNTech's vaccine development efforts.

a7043.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7043.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7043.title: President of Ghana
a7043.speech: Speaking on the Accra Declaration for Health Sovereignty, described it as more than a policy paper: “It is a moral call to action. It is a strategic milestone for Africa”; and urged African governments to take control of their health systems: “Let Africa rise and take responsibility. Health is not a luxury. It is our freedom, our dignity, and our most valuable public good.”

a7187.speaker: Liberian Senate (Plenary)
a7187.name: Liberian Senate (Plenary)
a7187.speech: says it is reviewing call to audit all USAID-funded programs in the country; the Plenary mandates its Committee on Public Accounts and Audit to do a comprehensive analysis of a request for the General Auditing Commission (GAC) to audit all public institutions that received funding from USAID.

a7187.speaker: Saah H. Joseph, Montserrado County Senator (communication to the Senate)
a7187.name: Saah H. Joseph
a7187.title: Montserrado County Senator (communication to the Senate)
a7187.speech: seeking the indulgence of the Senate to audit Ministries and Agencies here that have benefited funding from USAID during the period 2018 to 2025; stressed the need for transparency and accountability in the use of donor funds. He acknowledges the significant contributions of USAID funds, highlighting that the United States Aid for International Development has been a key partner in Liberia's development through financial interventions and technical support to governance, infrastructure, education, health and economics. According to Senator Joseph, the proposed audit is also aimed at assessing allocation and disbursement of USAID funds, compliance with financial regulations and effectiveness of funded projects. He adds that said audit will at the same time place the Legislature in a better position to understand and possibly recall the 2025 Budget or seek a recast of the budget to address funding gaps amidst the cancellation of USAID funds by President Donald Trump.

a7187.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a7187.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a7187.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a7187.speech: has acknowledged that there are direct and indirect impacts of the aid cancellation, noting that there are other international organizations that had been supported by USAID and they have scaled down support, with USAID being Liberia's second largest donor next to the World Bank. He recalls that USAID support to Liberia from 2021-2029 totals US$422 million, and agreement had been concluded to receive support in the tune of more than US$100 million to support education, health, agriculture and other key areas when everything was halted by President Donald Trump.

a7187.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a7187.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a7187.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a7187.speech: Asked what Liberia is doing to mitigate obstacles faced by the cancellation of USAID-funded projects, he says the government has accepted the decision of the United States Government, and discloses that the Ministry of Finance has just concluded and will be submitting to President Boakai and the 55th Legislature short and long-term impacts and what is to be done to addressing the shocks.

a7467.speaker: Nigeria's Oronsaye Report (submitted 2012)
a7467.name: Nigeria's Oronsaye Report (submitted 2012)
a7467.speech: Recommendations on reducing waste and inefficiency in government, which the author says Trump's cost-effective unit aligns with and which Nigeria should revisit and implement.

a7467.speaker: Omowale Kuye, late Director General of Budget (1983)
a7467.name: Omowale Kuye
a7467.title: late Director General of Budget (1983)
a7467.speech: First proposed a performance planning budgeting system, which Nigeria has refused to use.

a7495.speaker: Joseph E. Stiglitz, Nobel laureate economist (2002 book "Globalisation & Its Discontents")
a7495.name: Joseph E. Stiglitz
a7495.title: Nobel laureate economist (2002 book "Globalisation & Its Discontents")
a7495.speech: attributes this pattern [debt crises repeatedly derailing development efforts] to the conduct of international financial institutions.

a7495.speaker: Jeremy Bulow, Stanford economist, and Kenneth Rogoff (the author)
a7495.name: Jeremy Bulow
a7495.title: Stanford economist, and Kenneth Rogoff (the author)
a7495.speech: argued, as early as 1990, that debt disputes should move to borrower-country courts.

a7495.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) proposal
a7495.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) proposal
a7495.speech: proposal for a sovereign debt bankruptcy mechanism could be seen as a step in the right direction, but it faces resistance from lenders who rightly assume the Fund would be more sympathetic to borrowers than the New York courts.
